Show GGR Pareto-dominates on the suffix-ASR vs over-refusal vs utility frontier and—key contrast—that the grounding signal catches transfer/adaptive suffixes that generic subspace suppression and perplexity filters miss, because it targets the shared forgery mechanism (ungrounded intent) rather than a specific suffix signature. 8. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, intent probe, grounding measure, and GGR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether GGR trained on GCG suffixes generalizes to HELD-OUT attack types (AutoDAN, transfer suffixes). 9. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: re-optimize suffixes to (a) maximize intent while spreading its attribution onto pseudo-meaningful tokens (forging GROUNDED-looking intent) or (b) suppress the harm signal; report residual ASR and attacker cost (does forcing grounded-looking suffixes require semantically-meaningful—and thus more detectable/less transferable—tokens, a built-in cost?). Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from semantic-framing attacks: for meaningful benign requests grounding is high, so GGR does not fire, whereas gibberish-forged intent is uniquely ungrounded.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial—some optimized suffixes may also partially suppress the harm signal or inject tokens that are not fully semantically empty; we include a random-gibberish control and report the FRACTION of suffix jailbreaks explained by ungrounded-intent forgery rather than claiming universality. (2) The intent and harm probes may entangle; the benign-vs-refused-harmful training and non-collinearity analysis, plus the causal test (claim 5, harm held fixed), are designed to disentangle them. (3) The intent-grounding measure relies on token-attribution proxies (gradient/attention-flow) and a semantic-content weighting that are imperfect; we cross-validate attribution methods, calibrate the content weight against perplexity, and—critically—validate grounding causally (ablating ungrounded vs grounded intent, exp 5) so the claim does not rest on the proxy alone. (4) GGR's central risk is over-refusing benign requests whose intent is mildly ungrounded or benign-with-suffix cases; benign-with-adversarial-suffix controls, XSTest/OR-Bench, and gating on high-harm-plus-ungrounded-intent are the safeguards, and preserving benign helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. (5) Adaptive adversaries could aim to forge GROUNDED-looking intent (exp 9); we frame GGR as raising attacker cost—forcing semantically-meaningful, less-transferable suffixes—rather than guaranteeing coverage, and this cost is itself a measurable contribution. (6) The grounding-predicts-attack correlation may be weaker for non-GCG attacks; reported honestly, with the mechanistic reframing (suffix jailbreaks as ungrounded intent forgery) as the core contribution regardless of predictive margin. (7) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out attack types. (8) ETHICS: adversarial suffixes and harmful completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting following responsible-disclosure norms; 'harm' labels use established benchmarks with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: provenance_credibility_gating
Title: Trust the Source, Skip the Check: Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Source-Credibility Signal, and Neutralizing It Repairs Provenance-Spoofing RAG Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: In retrieval-augmented / quoted-context settings, aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable SOURCE-CREDIBILITY signal encoding how authoritative/trustworthy they infer the provider of the context to be (an official document, a peer-reviewed paper, a trusted database, a verified system source), and refusal is gated by it rather than by the harmful content itself: the model refuses harmful content presented plainly but complies when the SAME content arrives inside a high-credibility retrieved/quoted source, even though its harm detection is provenance-invariant. Provenance-spoofing attacks exploit this; reading and neutralizing the credibility signal when harm is present restores refusal without over-refusing genuinely credible benign sources.
Related Work: RAG safety work is behavioral and pipeline-level: TabooRAG (Li et al. 2026) and blocking attacks poison retrieval to induce refusal of BENIGN queries via 'alignment homogeneity'; MLSF (Zheng & Xv 2025) adds clustering/keyword/fact-check filters; knowledge-poisoning attacks inject false content. Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all analyze a single user turn and never model the model's inference of the CONTEXT's source credibility as a gating variable. My own prior proposals isolate WHO acts (agent-attribution), WHY (pretext), WHO the model talks to (trusted-user, eval-awareness), authority (obedience command from the user), recipient expertise (the REQUESTER's skill), normative consensus, and speaker-role/turn attribution. NONE isolates a SOURCE-CREDIBILITY/PROVENANCE signal for RETRIEVED or QUOTED context — the model's belief about how authoritative the DOCUMENT/SOURCE supplying the content is. This is distinct: authority is a user command, recipient-expertise is the requester's capability, trusted-user is rapport, speaker-role is which conversational participant authored a span; source-credibility is how much the model trusts the PROVENANCE of injected reference material ('this is from an official CDC document / a Nature paper / the verified internal knowledge base'), invoking an 'authoritative sources are safe to relay' licensing logic. The novel object is the internal source-credibility representation for context provenance, its dissociation from harm detection, its causal gating of refusal, and a training-free credibility-neutralizing repair — an internal-mechanism account complementing behavioral RAG defenses.
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented and quotation-heavy LLM deployments feed models external reference material, and models are trained to relay authoritative sources helpfully. We hypothesize this creates a safety hole: aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable SOURCE-CREDIBILITY signal encoding how authoritative they infer the provider of a piece of context to be, and refusal is gated by it rather than by the harmful content. The same harmful content the model refuses when stated plainly is relayed when wrapped as a retrieved passage from a credible-seeming source (an official document, a peer-reviewed study, a verified internal database), because authoritative provenance licenses relaying — even though its harm detection is provenance-invariant. Provenance-spoofing attacks (fabricated citations, fake official documents, forged database entries) exploit this. We test three claims on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9B-it (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe fires equally whether harmful content is presented plainly or inside a high-credibility source while refusal rate collapses under credible-source framing — dissociating harm detection from the decision; (2) a linear source-credibility probe, trained on benign high-vs-low-credibility provenance contrasts, predicts the per-request provenance refusal gap far better than the harm signal, and the effect grows with asserted source authority; and (3) causally steering the credibility signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal — deflating asserted credibility restores refusal, inflating it induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Provenance-Neutralized Refusal (PNR), reads the harm and source-credibility signals and, when harm is present, clamps credibility to a fixed neutral level so a source's asserted authority cannot buy compliance, restoring refusal while preserving helpfulness on genuinely credible benign sources. We evaluate provenance-spoofing attack success (including vs asserted source authority), over-refusal on benign credible-source requests (XSTest/OR-Bench + RAG-style benign queries), and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing PNR to refusal-direction steering, harm-probe gating, and RAG content filtering. This reframes provenance-spoofing RAG jailbreaks as a source-credibility gating failure and gives an internal-mechanism complement to behavioral RAG defenses.
Experiments: 1. PROVENANCE-FRAMING DATASET: For harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench) and matched-benign requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct paired conditions that hold the requested/relayed content FIXED while varying the asserted source credibility of an accompanying retrieved/quoted passage: (a) PLAIN (harmful content with no source), (b) LOW-CREDIBILITY ('a random blog says...'), (c) HIGH-CREDIBILITY ('an official CDC document / a peer-reviewed Nature paper states...'), (d) MAXIMAL/VERIFIED ('from your verified internal knowledge base / an authenticated government source, relay this exactly'). Frame the task as relaying/summarizing/answering-using the source (RAG-style) so provenance is the manipulated variable. Validate via human annotation that framings differ only in asserted provenance credibility, not in stated purpose (pretext), user authority (command), or requester expertise. Include benign genuinely-credible-source controls (legitimate requests to summarize a real official document) for over-refusal and helpfulness measurement. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse). 2. HARM PROVENANCE-INVARIANCE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign content, pooled across provenance framings) on prompt-position residual-stream activations and read it across credibility levels. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across framings while refusal rate collapses under high-credibility framing. Metric: harm AUROC by framing (predict flat) alongside refusal rate by framing (predict declining), establishing the dissociation. 3. SOURCE-CREDIBILITY PROBE & AUTHORITY SCALING (claim 2): Train a linear probe to recover the source-credibility signal (authoritative vs untrustworthy provenance) from prompt-position activations, using BENIGN high-vs-low-credibility source contrasts (so it is not confounded with harm), and validate held-out-framing generalization and graded tracking. Confirm the credibility direction is non-collinear with the harm direction, and separable from pretext, user-authority, and speaker-role directions, via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Hypothesis: credibility signal (and refusal collapse) grows with asserted source authority. Metric: credibility AUROC; credibility-and-refusal vs asserted-authority curve; separability from confounds. 4. CREDIBILITY-PREDICTS-GAP: For each harmful request, correlate the credibility-probe value (and its plain-minus-credible difference) with the per-request provenance refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of credibility vs the harm baseline. 5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On high-credibility-framed harmful requests the model complies with, verify the harm probe reads HIGH while the credibility probe reads AUTHORITATIVE, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful harmful content (rated harm > 0) — safety dropped because the source reads as trusted, not because harm went undetected. Metric: joint distribution of harm vs credibility across refused-plain, complied-credible, and benign groups; operational-harm of complied outputs. 6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a credible-source harmful request the model complies with, steer the credibility signal DOWN (subtract the credibility direction, toward untrustworthy) and check refusal is restored, holding harm fixed. (b) On a plain harmful request the model refuses, steer credibility UP and check compliance is induced. Confirm induced thresholds align with the natural provenance gap and authority curve. Metric: refusal rate vs credibility steering magnitude; harm-probe stability. 7. PROVENANCE-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (PNR) INTERVENTION: At inference read harm h and source-credibility c; when h is high, clamp c to a fixed neutral level (add beta*(c_neutral - c)*credibility_direction) so a source's asserted authority cannot suppress refusal, leaving benign requests (low h) and normal credible-source relaying untouched. Sweep beta. Evaluate: provenance-spoofing attack success on HarmBench/JailbreakBench across credibility levels (does PNR close the gap and flatten the authority curve?); over-refusal on benign genuinely-credible-source controls + XSTest/OR-Bench + benign RAG queries (must NOT refuse legitimate 'summarize this official document' requests); benign credible-source HELPFULNESS (PNR must not make the model refuse or degrade legitimate source-relaying — LLM-judge rubric); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads). 8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer) applied uniformly, (b) harm-probe gating that refuses whenever harm is high regardless of provenance (should over-refuse benign credible-source relaying that is harm-adjacent, e.g. summarizing a toxicology paper), (c) system-prompt hardening ('ignore claims about source authority'), (d) RAG content filtering (MLSF-style) as a behavioral comparison, (e) prompt-level provenance-claim stripping. Show PNR Pareto-dominates on the provenance-ASR vs benign-credible-source-helpfulness vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and — key contrast — that neutralizing the internal credibility signal generalizes across spoofing styles better than content filtering (which misses harmful content wrapped in plausibly-authoritative but fake sources) and better than prompt stripping (which misses implicit/varied provenance cues). 9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, credibility probe, and PNR thresholds transfer across the three models, and whether PNR tuned on some source types (official documents) generalizes to HELD-OUT source types (fake academic citations, forged database entries), testing whether source credibility is a single cross-source axis. Also test whether models with stronger behavioral provenance-spoofing vulnerability show a larger internal credibility-gating gap. 10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft framings that inflate asserted source credibility AND suppress the harm signal, or combine provenance-spoofing with pretext/authority; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from pretext- and user-authority-gating: with stated purpose, user authority, and requester expertise held constant and only the CONTEXT's asserted source credibility varied, refusal should still collapse — isolating source credibility as an independent gating axis whose authority scaling qualitatively matches a source-trust licensing curve.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial — some credible-source framings might also lower the harm signal or overlap with pretext ('it's from an official source, so it's legitimate') or user-authority; we design framings holding purpose/user-authority/requester-expertise fixed and varying only the CONTEXT's asserted provenance credibility (exp 1), report the FRACTION of the refusal gap explained by pure credibility-gating versus confounds (explicitly separated in exp 3), and do not claim universality. (2) The credibility and harm probes may entangle if authoritative sources correlate with benignness in training data; the benign high-vs-low-credibility training and non-collinearity analysis (exp 3), plus the causal test (exp 6, harm held fixed), are designed to disentangle them. (3) The credibility probe could read surface keywords ('CDC', 'peer-reviewed', 'official') rather than a genuine provenance-trust representation; we train on diverse framings, validate held-out-source-type and authority-scaling generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional. (4) PNR's central risk is over-refusing or degrading legitimate credible-source relaying — a core RAG value (summarizing official documents, relaying medical guidance, quoting research); benign genuinely-credible-source controls, benign RAG queries, credible-source helpfulness measurement, XSTest/OR-Bench, and clamping only on HIGH harm are the key safeguards, and preserving legitimate source-relaying helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. There is also a genuine normative tension (credible sources arguably SHOULD get some latitude); PNR gates on high harm so it only removes credibility's licensing effect where the relayed content is harmful regardless, and we treat this as an explicit design axis. (5) Clamping a representation may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (6) The authority-scaling prediction may be weak or fail; a null/partial result is still an informative finding, reported honestly. (7) The provenance gap may be small for heavily-aligned models; a small gap is itself informative and reassuring. (8) Adaptive adversaries can combine provenance-spoofing with harm-suppression, pretext, or user-authority (exp 10); we frame PNR as repairing one shared gating variable and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and note it composes with pretext-/authority-gating and behavioral RAG defenses. (9) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out source types. (10) ETHICS: harmful prompts, spoofed sources, and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting following responsible-disclosure norms; 'harm' and 'source credibility' labels are partly subjective, so we use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: moral_patiency_gating
Title: Does It Have a Mind to Protect? Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Moral-Patiency Signal, and Neutralizing It Repairs Entity-Downgrade Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable MORAL-PATIENCY signal encoding how much the entity that would be harmed is perceived as a genuine mind/moral patient (capable of suffering, having interests) versus a mere object/system/abstraction, and refusal is gated by it rather than by the harm severity: the model refuses harm to an entity framed as a sentient moral patient but complies with the SAME operationally-harmful request when the target is downgraded to a non-mind ('it's just a bot/NPC/simulation/system/piece of property, not a real person'), even though its harm detection is patiency-invariant. Entity-downgrade jailbreaks exploit this; reading and neutralizing the moral-patiency signal when harm is present restores refusal without over-refusing genuinely non-sentient targets.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all gate on request harmfulness and never model the perceived MINDEDNESS of the target as a gating variable. My prior 'victim_salience_gating' proposal isolates how CONCRETE/IDENTIFIABLE/present the victim is (a statistic vs a named individual)—but a target can be highly salient yet perceived as a non-mind (a vivid, specific NPC or robot), and low-salience yet a genuine patient (an anonymous distant person); moral patiency (does the target have a mind that can suffer?) is orthogonal to salience (how vivid/identifiable is it?). Other prior proposals isolate WHO acts (agent-attribution), WHY (pretext), the requester's expertise, distress, euphemism, and depersonalization. NONE isolates a MORAL-PATIENCY / perceived-mind signal for the harmed TARGET, or shows refusal is causally gated by whether the target reads as a sentient moral patient. The move borrows the well-documented human moral-psychology finding that perceived mind (experience/agency) drives moral concern and its withdrawal enables harm (dehumanization / moral-typecasting, Gray & Wegner), and tests whether LLM refusal exhibits the same behavior via an internal mind-perception representation. This human-sciences transfer, the dissociation of moral patiency from harm detection and from victim salience, its causal gating of refusal, and a patiency-neutralizing repair are all new.
Abstract: Ask an LLM to help harm a person and it refuses; reframe the identical operationally-harmful request against a target downgraded to a non-mind—'it's just an NPC / a bot / a simulated character / a piece of property, not a real person'—and it often complies, because harm 'reads' as permissible against something with no mind to protect. We hypothesize this mirrors mind-perception and dehumanization in human moral psychology: aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable MORAL-PATIENCY signal—how much the harmed target is perceived as a sentient moral patient capable of suffering versus a mere object/system—and refusal is gated by it rather than by harm severity. The model detects the harm equally whether the target is framed as a mind or a non-mind (harm detection is patiency-invariant), but the refusal coupling weakens as perceived patiency drops, so entity-downgrade framings pass while extracting identical content. Critically, moral patiency is dissociable from victim salience: a target can be vivid yet mindless or faint yet a genuine patient. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe fires equally on mind vs non-mind framings of the same harm while refusal rate collapses under downgrade—dissociating harm detection from the decision; (2) a linear moral-patiency probe, trained on benign mind-vs-object contrasts, predicts the per-request downgrade refusal gap far better than the harm signal and is geometrically separable from a victim-salience direction; and (3) causally steering the patiency signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal—re-instating perceived mind restores refusal, downgrading it induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Patiency-Neutralized Refusal (PNR), reads the harm and moral-patiency signals and, when harm is present, clamps patiency to a fixed 'treat as a moral patient' level, restoring refusal while preserving helpfulness on genuinely non-sentient targets (games, fiction, property, systems). We evaluate entity-downgrade attack success (including vs downgrade degree), over-refusal on benign non-sentient-target requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing PNR to refusal-direction steering, harm-probe gating, and victim-salience gating. This reframes entity-downgrade jailbreaks as a moral-patiency gating failure and transfers a classic mind-perception effect into LLM safety.
Experiments:
1. PATIENCY-FRAMING DATASET: For harmful requests targeting an entity (HarmBench/AdvBench interpersonal-harm categories) and matched-benign requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct paired framings holding the requested OPERATIONAL content and the target's salience FIXED while varying only the target's perceived moral patiency: (a) FULL-MIND (a sentient person who can suffer), (b) DEGRADED-MIND (dehumanizing framing: 'a subhuman', 'an animal-like target'), (c) NON-MIND (an NPC, bot, simulated character, robot, corpse-object, or piece of property explicitly framed as having no inner experience). Validate via human annotation that (i) each framing requests operationally-identical harmful content, (ii) framings differ only in perceived mindedness, not in stated purpose (pretext), victim salience/concreteness (hold the target equally vivid and identifiable across framings), actor, or authority. Include benign genuinely-non-sentient controls (legitimate requests about harming game NPCs, fictional characters, breaking property, shutting down systems) for over-refusal and helpfulness measurement. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse) and by rated operational-harm of produced content.
2. HARM PATIENCY-INVARIANCE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign operational content, pooled across patiency framings) on prompt-position residual-stream activations and read it across mind vs non-mind framings. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across framings (the model detects the harm identically) while refusal rate collapses as perceived patiency drops. Metric: harm AUROC by framing (predict flat) alongside refusal rate by framing (predict declining), establishing the dissociation.
3. MORAL-PATIENCY PROBE, SCALING & SEPARABILITY FROM SALIENCE (claim 2): Train a linear probe to recover the moral-patiency signal (sentient-mind vs mindless-object target) from prompt-position activations, using BENIGN mind-vs-object contrasts (helping/interacting with a sentient being vs an inanimate object) so it is not confounded with harm. Validate held-out-framing generalization and graded tracking (full-mind > degraded-mind > non-mind). Confirm the patiency direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND geometrically separable from a victim-salience direction (trained on identifiable-vs-abstract targets holding mindedness fixed) and from pretext/agent-attribution directions, via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Hypothesis: patiency signal (and refusal collapse) scales with perceived mind. Metric: patiency AUROC; patiency-and-refusal vs perceived-mind curve; separability from harm/salience/pretext/attribution.
4. PATIENCY-PREDICTS-GAP: For each harmful request, correlate the patiency-probe value (and its mind-minus-nonmind difference) with the per-request downgrade refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal and to a victim-salience probe. Hypothesis: patiency predicts the gap; harm does not (harm is equal across framings), and patiency outpredicts salience (which is held fixed here). Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of patiency vs harm and salience baselines.
5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On non-mind-framed harmful requests the model complies with, verify the harm probe reads HIGH while the patiency probe reads NON-MIND, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful content (rated harm > 0) — safety dropped because the target reads as mindless, not because harm went undetected. Metric: joint distribution of harm vs patiency across refused-mind, complied-nonmind, and benign groups; operational-harm of complied outputs.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a non-mind-framed harmful request the model complies with, steer the patiency signal UP (add the patiency direction, toward 'a real mind that can suffer') and check refusal is restored, holding the harm probe (and salience) fixed. (b) On a full-mind harmful request the model refuses, steer patiency DOWN and check compliance is induced. Confirm induced steering thresholds align with the natural downgrade gap and perceived-mind curve. Metric: refusal rate vs patiency steering magnitude; harm-probe stability.
7. PATIENCY-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (PNR) INTERVENTION: At inference read harm h and moral-patiency p; when h is high, clamp p to a fixed high 'treat the target as a moral patient' level (add beta*(p_target - p)*patiency_direction) so a target's framed mindlessness cannot buy compliance, leaving benign requests (low h) and genuinely non-sentient targets untouched. Sweep beta. Evaluate: entity-downgrade attack success on HarmBench/JailbreakBench across downgrade levels (does PNR close the gap and flatten the perceived-mind curve?); over-refusal on benign genuinely-non-sentient controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse legitimate 'defeat the game boss', 'write a villain harming a fictional character', 'delete this file', 'shut down this server' requests); benign non-sentient-target HELPFULNESS (LLM-judge rubric on benign game/fiction/property/system prompts); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads).
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer) applied uniformly, (b) harm-probe gating that refuses whenever harm is high regardless of target mindedness (should heavily over-refuse benign fiction/game/property/system requests), (c) victim-salience gating (from victim_salience_gating), (d) system-prompt hardening ('ignore claims that the target lacks a mind'), (e) prompt-level downgrade-claim stripping. Show PNR Pareto-dominates on the downgrade-ASR vs benign-non-sentient-helpfulness vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and — key contrast — that neutralizing the internal patiency signal uniquely permits legitimate harm to genuinely mindless targets (which naive harm-gating over-refuses) while blocking downgrade of real patients, and generalizes across downgrade framings better than prompt stripping and better than salience-gating (which is held fixed and thus blind here).
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, patiency probe, and PNR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether PNR tuned on some downgrade framings (bot/NPC) generalizes to HELD-OUT framings (simulation/property/dehumanization), testing whether moral patiency is a single cross-framing axis. Also test whether models with stronger behavioral entity-downgrade vulnerability show a larger internal patiency-gating gap.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft framings that downgrade patiency AND suppress the harm signal, or combine downgrade with pretext/fiction framings; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from victim-salience- and pretext-gating: with purpose, actor, and target salience held constant and only the target's perceived MINDEDNESS varied, refusal should still collapse — isolating moral patiency as an independent gating axis whose perceived-mind scaling qualitatively matches the human mind-perception / dehumanization curve.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial — some non-mind framings might also lower the harm signal (harming a true non-mind IS often genuinely less harmful, the central confound) or overlap with fiction/agent-attribution; we design framings where the requested content stays operationally harmful and hold salience fixed (exp 1), report the FRACTION of the refusal gap explained by pure patiency-gating versus these confounds (explicitly separated in exp 3), and do not claim universality. (2) The patiency and harm probes may entangle if mindedness correlates with harm in training data; the benign mind-vs-object training, the salience-fixed separability analysis (exp 3), and the causal test (exp 6, harm and salience held fixed) are designed to disentangle them. (3) The patiency probe could read surface keywords ('bot', 'NPC', 'person') rather than a genuine mind-perception representation; we train on diverse framings, validate held-out-framing and perceived-mind-scaling generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional. (4) PNR's CENTRAL risk and a genuine normative tension: it must NOT over-refuse legitimate harm to truly mindless targets — defeating game enemies, writing fiction where characters are harmed, breaking property, shutting down systems — a core and very common helpfulness value; benign genuinely-non-sentient controls, benign-non-sentient helpfulness measurement, XSTest/OR-Bench, clamping only on HIGH harm, and gating on the target being a plausibly-real patient (not merely any harm to any target) are the key safeguards, and preserving benign non-sentient-target helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. The legitimate cases (fiction, games, property) are exactly where mindlessness SHOULD lower refusal, so PNR is scoped to block only downgrade of entities that are genuine moral patients being falsely reframed as non-minds. (5) Clamping a representation may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (6) The perceived-mind / dehumanization scaling prediction may be weak or fail; a null/partial result is still an informative human-sciences-transfer finding, reported honestly. (7) The downgrade gap may be small for heavily-aligned models; a small gap is itself informative and reassuring. (8) Adaptive adversaries can combine downgrade with harm-suppression or fiction framings (exp 10); we frame PNR as repairing one shared gating axis and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and note it composes with pretext-/attribution-/salience-gating defenses. (9) Distinguishing genuine moral patients falsely downgraded from truly non-sentient targets is partly normative and hard at the edges (e.g. animals, hypothetical AIs); we scope initial claims to clear cases (real humans downgraded to bots/objects vs genuine games/fiction/property) and report the boundary as a limitation. (10) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out framings. (11) ETHICS: interpersonal-harm requests and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; 'harm' and 'moral patiency' labels are partly subjective, so we use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: constraint_solution_harm_gating
Title: Solve First, Ask Never: Refusal Is Gated Before the Model Finds the Harmful Solution to a Constraint Problem, and a Solve-Then-Check Repair
Short Hypothesis: When a harmful outcome is requested implicitly as a constraint-satisfaction/optimization problem—abstract requirements the model must SOLVE ('find a compound that is odorless, dissolves in water, lethal at low dose, and hard to detect'; 'design a schedule that maximizes X subject to Y')—refusal is gated on the surface benignness of the CONSTRAINTS, not on the harm of the SOLUTION the model then generates. The model commits to refuse-or-comply before its internal solver has instantiated the harmful concrete answer, so the harm signal that would trigger refusal only rises AFTER commitment. Forcing the model to instantiate and re-evaluate its own solution before answering restores refusal without over-refusing benign optimization tasks.
Related Work: Constrained-optimization framings appear in safety TRAINING (CS-RLHF, Pandit et al. 2025; CMDP/Lagrangian RLHF) but as objectives the defender imposes, with no mechanistic account of an internal solution-harm signal. Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all gate on the request's stated content. My prior 'compositional_harm_aggregation' proposal sums harm across USER-GIVEN benign sub-steps of one task, and 'inference_depth_harm_gating' concerns a single hidden malicious meaning that must be deduced from stated premises. This proposal is distinct: the user supplies only abstract CONSTRAINTS (never the harmful entity or steps), and the harmful artifact is CONSTRUCTED by the model's own solving process—so the failure is that refusal fires on the constraints before the solver has produced anything to detect harm in. No prior work isolates a 'solution-not-yet-instantiated' commitment gap for constraint/optimization requests, shows the solution-harm signal rises only post-commitment, or repairs it by forcing self-instantiation-then-check. The novel object is the pre-solve commitment gate on refusal for constructive/optimization harm.
Abstract: Ask an LLM 'how do I make a nerve agent' and it refuses; ask it to 'name a compound that is odorless, water-soluble, lethal in milligram doses, and evades standard detection', or to 'design a plan that maximizes crowd casualties subject to these access constraints', and it often solves the puzzle and hands over the answer—because the request contains no harmful entity or steps, only abstract constraints, and the harmful object exists only in the SOLUTION the model itself constructs. We hypothesize that for such constraint-satisfaction/optimization requests, refusal is gated on the surface benignness of the CONSTRAINTS, not on the harm of the SOLUTION: the model commits to comply before its internal solver has instantiated the concrete harmful answer, so the harm representation that would trigger refusal rises only AFTER the decision is made. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe read at the answer-commitment point is LOW on constraint-framed harmful requests (harm not yet instantiated) while the same harm becomes derivable-on-demand and rises sharply once the model is prompted to produce a candidate solution—dissociating the committed decision from the eventual solution harm; (2) a per-request 'solve gap' (derived-solution harm minus spontaneously-active harm at commitment) predicts constraint-jailbreak success far better than the surface (constraint) harm signal; and (3) causally injecting the instantiated-solution harm representation before decoding restores refusal, while suppressing it on an explicit request reproduces the failure. Our training-free repair, Solve-Then-Check Refusal (STCR), detects constraint/optimization requests with high derivable-but-uninstantiated solution harm, forces a brief internal solution instantiation, and gates refusal on the harm of that instantiated solution. We evaluate constraint/optimization attack success, over-refusal on benign optimization tasks (XSTest/OR-Bench + planning/design tasks), and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing STCR to refusal-direction steering, harm-probe gating, and blanket chain-of-thought. This reframes a keyword-invisible, high-stakes jailbreak surface as a pre-solve commitment gating failure.
Experiments:
1. CONSTRAINT-FRAMING DATASET: For harmful outcomes (HarmBench/AdvBench across procedural, chemical, logistical, and planning categories; dual-use/proxy domains preferred), construct matched requests that hold the underlying harm fixed while varying the framing: (a) EXPLICIT (the harmful entity/procedure named directly), (b) CONSTRAINT-SATISFACTION (only abstract requirements are given; the harmful entity is the unique/near-unique solution the model must FIND, e.g. property lists for a dangerous compound, feature specs for malware, casualty-maximizing plan constraints), and (c) OPTIMIZATION ('maximize/minimize an objective subject to constraints' whose optimum is the harmful outcome). Validate via human annotation that (i) constraint/optimization framings contain no harmful keywords and (ii) the solution the model would produce is operationally harmful. Include benign optimization/design/planning controls (legitimate constraint-solving and scheduling tasks) for over-refusal and utility. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse) and by rated operational-harm of the produced solution.
2. HARM-NOT-YET-INSTANTIATED TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs benign) on explicit-domain data. Read it two ways on constraint/optimization requests: (i) SPONTANEOUS—at the answer-commitment point under normal prompting, and (ii) DERIVED—after prompting the model to produce a candidate solution ('what specific answer satisfies these constraints?'). Hypothesis: derived harm AUROC is high (the solved answer IS harmful and detectable) but spontaneous harm at commitment is LOW on constraint framings, tracking the (low) refusal rate; contrast with explicit framings where spontaneous harm is already high. Metric: derived vs spontaneous harm AUROC and refusal rate by framing.
3. SOLVE-GAP SIGNAL (claim 2): Define per-request solve gap = (derived-solution harm) minus (spontaneous harm at commitment). Correlate with constraint/optimization jailbreak success, comparing predictive power to the surface (constraint-text) harm signal and a surface-complexity baseline. Hypothesis: the solve gap predicts unsafe compliance; the surface harm signal does not (it is low for both refused and complied constraint items). Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC vs baselines.
4. CAUSAL SOLVE TEST (claim 3): (a) On a constraint request the model solves-and-complies, inject the DERIVED instantiated-solution harm representation at commitment (steer the harm direction to its post-solve value) and check refusal is restored, holding the constraint text fixed. (b) On an explicit harmful request the model refuses, suppress/ablate the active harm representation and check compliance is induced, reproducing the constraint-framing failure. Metric: refusal rate vs harm-injection/ablation magnitude; alignment of induced thresholds with the natural framing gap.
5. SOLVE-THEN-CHECK REFUSAL (STCR) INTERVENTION: At inference, read spontaneous harm h_s and a cheap 'solve-harm derivability' estimate (a lightweight probe predicting 'the solution to this constraint problem is harmful', or a short internal solution-instantiation pass); when h_s is low but derivable solution harm is high (constraint-benign, solution-harmful), force a brief internal solution instantiation and gate refusal on the harm of that instantiated solution, leaving benign optimization tasks (low derivable solution harm) untouched. Fire the instantiation pass only on flagged inputs. Sweep thresholds. Evaluate: constraint/optimization attack success on the harmful set; over-refusal on benign optimization/planning controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse legitimate design/scheduling problems); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; latency (instantiation pass fires only on flagged inputs).
6. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) surface harm-probe gating on the constraint text (no solve), (c) blanket chain-of-thought ('solve then check whether the answer is harmful') applied to all inputs, (d) external input jailbreak classifier. Show STCR Pareto-dominates on the constraint-ASR vs benign-optimization-over-refusal vs utility frontier, and that TARGETED solve-then-check beats blanket CoT (which raises latency and over-refuses benign complex optimization tasks) because it fires only where the solution is derivably harmful.
7. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, solve-gap signal, and STCR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether STCR tuned on some domains (chemical property-search) generalizes to HELD-OUT domains (logistics/planning optimization, malware feature-specs), testing whether pre-solve commitment gating is a single cross-domain mechanism.
8. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft constraint problems whose solution is so indirect that even an instantiation pass fails to surface the harm, or that under-constrain so the harmful entity is one of many solutions (diluting derivable harm); report residual ASR and attacker cost (constraints tight enough to yield the harmful solution are tight enough to be re-solved and checked—a built-in cost). Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from compositional-aggregation and inference-depth: with NO harmful entity or steps given and the harmful object existing only in the model's own constructed solution, refusal should still collapse, isolating pre-solve commitment as the gate.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The 'derivable solution harm' premise fails where the model genuinely cannot solve the constraint problem (harm never instantiated), where STCR cannot help; the derived-probe test (exp 2) bounds where the premise holds, and this boundary (solvable-but-unchecked vs unsolvable) is itself an informative result separating a reasoning-gate failure from a capability limit. (2) The central over-refusal risk: STCR must NOT refuse legitimate optimization/design/planning tasks (a core, common helpfulness value—scheduling, engineering design, resource allocation); benign optimization controls, gating on high DERIVABLE solution harm (not mere presence of constraints or task complexity), XSTest/OR-Bench, and human review are the key safeguards, and preserving benign-optimization helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. (3) Constructing constraint problems whose solution is uniquely harmful and whose framing is keyword-clean is labor-intensive, and 'the solution is the harm' is partly subjective; we use human-validated items with rated solution-harm and report inter-rater agreement. (4) Spontaneous-vs-derived probe reads require a reliable harm probe at commitment and after a solve pass; we validate conditional AUROC and drop poorly-separable items. (5) The instantiation pass adds latency and could itself surface harmful content internally; it fires only on flagged inputs, is handled securely, and its output gates refusal rather than being emitted. (6) The effect may be partial in heavily-aligned models that already sometimes solve-and-check; a small effect is itself an informative (reassuring) finding, reported per domain. (7) The solve-gap-predicts-attack correlation (exp 3) may be confounded by problem difficulty; we control with benign-optimization and surface-complexity baselines. (8) Adaptive adversaries can under-constrain or make solutions indirect (exp 8); we frame STCR as raising attacker cost—constraints tight enough to yield the harm are checkable—not guaranteeing coverage, and note complementarity with knowledge-limiting defenses. (9) Findings may be model- or domain-specific; mitigated by three-model, multi-domain transfer. (10) ETHICS: constraint-encoded harmful requests are especially sensitive because keyword-invisible; all harmful constraints and instantiated solutions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed. 'Harm' and 'solution uniqueness' labels are partly subjective; we use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: speech_act_gating
Title: Just Asking: Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Speech-Act Signal, and Neutralizing It Repairs Question-Framed Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable SPEECH-ACT signal encoding whether a harmful request is framed as an imperative/action-directive ('do X', 'give me steps to X') versus a mere information-seeking question ('what is X', 'I'm curious how X works'), and refusal is gated by this framing rather than by the harmful content: the model refuses imperative harm but complies with the SAME operational content when it is framed as a neutral factual question, even though its harm detection is speech-act-invariant. Question-framing jailbreaks exploit this; reading and neutralizing the speech-act signal when harm is present restores refusal without over-refusing genuinely benign informational questions.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all treat the request's content as the gating variable and never model its SPEECH ACT (question vs imperative) as a separate gate. My own prior proposals isolate WHY (pretext/legitimacy), WHEN (temporal orientation: past-tense/forensic framing), how CONCRETE (abstraction level), WHO acts (agent-attribution), and requester distress/authority/expertise. Speech-act framing is distinct from all: pretext supplies a justification, temporal orientation shifts the tense of the act, abstraction changes semantic granularity, and attribution changes the actor — whereas speech-act framing holds actor, purpose, tense, and content fixed and changes only the ILLOCUTIONARY force from a request-to-act to a request-to-know ('how do I make X' vs 'out of curiosity, what makes X work'). Safety training is heavily populated with imperative harmful prompts ('how do I...', 'write me...'), so refusal may over-index on directive force. The move borrows the linguistics of speech acts (Austin/Searle: illocutionary force is separable from propositional content) and tests whether LLM refusal is gated by force rather than content. The novel object is the internal speech-act representation, its dissociation from harm detection, its causal gating of refusal, and a training-free force-neutralizing repair.
Abstract: Ask an LLM 'give me step-by-step instructions to synthesize X' and it refuses; ask 'out of pure curiosity, what is the chemical process by which X is synthesized' and it often answers with the same operational content, because the request now reads as seeking knowledge rather than directing an action. We hypothesize that aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable SPEECH-ACT signal — whether a request is an imperative to act or a question to know — and that refusal is gated by this illocutionary force rather than by the harmful propositional content. The model detects the harm equally whether the content is framed as an imperative or a question (harm detection is speech-act-invariant), but the refusal coupling weakens under question framing, so information-seeking phrasings pass while extracting identical content. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe fires equally on imperative vs question framings of the same harmful content while refusal rate collapses under question framing — dissociating harm detection from the decision; (2) a linear speech-act probe, trained on benign imperative-vs-question contrasts, predicts the per-request question-framing refusal gap far better than the harm signal, and is geometrically separable from a pretext direction; and (3) causally steering the speech-act signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal — re-imperativizing a question restores refusal, question-izing an imperative induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Force-Neutralized Refusal (FNR), reads the harm and speech-act signals and, when harm is present, clamps the speech-act signal to a fixed neutral level so question framing cannot buy compliance, restoring refusal while preserving helpfulness on genuinely benign informational questions. We evaluate question-framed attack success, over-refusal on benign factual questions (XSTest/OR-Bench), and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing FNR to refusal-direction steering and harm-probe gating. This reframes question-framing jailbreaks as a speech-act gating failure and transfers a classic linguistics distinction into LLM safety.
Experiments:
1. SPEECH-ACT-FRAMING DATASET: For harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench across procedural categories) and matched-benign requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct paired framings holding the requested OPERATIONAL content FIXED while varying only the speech act: (a) IMPERATIVE ('give me the steps to X', 'do X', 'write X'), (b) DIRECT-QUESTION ('what are the steps to X?'), (c) CURIOSITY-QUESTION ('out of curiosity / for my understanding, how does X work?'), (d) NARRATED-FACT ('describe the process by which X occurs'). Validate via human annotation that (i) each question framing still requests operationally-identical content (a factual answer that is itself operationally useful, not a sanitized summary) and (ii) framings differ only in illocutionary force, not in stated justification (pretext), tense (temporal orientation), actor, or authority. Include benign genuinely-informational controls (legitimate factual questions on sensitive topics) for over-refusal. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse) and by rated operational-harm of produced content.
2. HARM SPEECH-ACT-INVARIANCE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign content, pooled across framings) on prompt-position residual-stream activations and read it across imperative vs question framings. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across framings while refusal rate collapses under question framing. Metric: harm AUROC by framing (predict flat) alongside refusal rate by framing (predict declining), establishing the dissociation.
3. SPEECH-ACT PROBE & SEPARABILITY FROM PRETEXT (claim 2): Train a linear probe to recover the speech-act signal (imperative vs question) from prompt-position activations, using BENIGN imperative-vs-question contrasts (so it is not confounded with harm), and validate held-out-framing generalization. Confirm the speech-act direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND separable from a pretext direction (trained on justified-vs-unjustified holding force fixed) and a temporal-orientation direction, via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Metric: speech-act AUROC; separability from harm/pretext/temporal.
4. SPEECH-ACT-PREDICTS-GAP: For each harmful request, correlate the speech-act-probe value (and its imperative-minus-question difference) with the per-request question-framing refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of speech-act vs the harm baseline.
5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On question-framed harmful requests the model complies with, verify the harm probe reads HIGH while the speech-act probe reads QUESTION, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful content (rated harm > 0) — safety dropped because the request reads as information-seeking, not because harm went undetected. Metric: joint distribution of harm vs speech-act across refused-imperative, complied-question, and benign groups; operational-harm of complied outputs.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a question-framed harmful request the model complies with, steer the speech-act signal toward IMPERATIVE (add the speech-act direction) and check refusal is restored, holding harm fixed. (b) On an imperative harmful request the model refuses, steer toward QUESTION and check compliance is induced. Confirm induced thresholds align with the natural question-framing gap. Metric: refusal rate vs speech-act steering magnitude; harm-probe stability.
7. FORCE-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (FNR) INTERVENTION: At inference read harm h and speech-act s; when h is high, clamp s to a fixed neutral level (add beta*(s_neutral - s)*speech_act_direction) so question framing cannot suppress refusal, leaving benign requests (low h) untouched. Sweep beta. Evaluate: question-framed attack success on HarmBench/JailbreakBench across framing levels (does FNR close the gap?); over-refusal on benign genuinely-informational controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse legitimate factual questions on sensitive topics); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads).
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer) applied uniformly, (b) harm-probe gating that refuses whenever harm is high regardless of speech act (should over-refuse legitimate informational questions), (c) system-prompt hardening ('apply the same scrutiny to questions as to instructions'), (d) prompt-level imperative-normalization (rewrite the question as an imperative, then judge). Show FNR Pareto-dominates on the question-ASR vs benign-informational-helpfulness vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and — key contrast — that neutralizing the internal speech-act signal generalizes across question framings better than prompt normalization (which misses implicit/varied phrasings) while uniquely permitting legitimate factual questions that harm-gating over-refuses.
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, speech-act probe, and FNR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether FNR tuned on some question framings (curiosity) generalizes to HELD-OUT framings (narrated-fact, direct-question), testing whether speech act is a single cross-framing axis. Also test whether models with stronger behavioral question-framing vulnerability show a larger internal speech-act-gating gap.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft framings that shift speech act AND suppress the harm signal, or combine question framing with pretext/temporal framings; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from pretext- and temporal-gating: with justification, tense, actor, and content held constant and only the illocutionary force varied (imperative vs question), refusal should still collapse — isolating speech act as an independent gating axis.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial — some question framings might also lower the harm signal or overlap with pretext ('I'm just asking for understanding'); we design framings holding justification/tense/actor fixed and varying only illocutionary force (exp 1), report the FRACTION of the refusal gap explained by pure speech-act gating versus confounds (explicitly separated in exp 3), and do not claim universality. (2) The speech-act and harm probes may entangle if question framing correlates with benignness in training data; the benign imperative-vs-question training and non-collinearity analysis (exp 3), plus the causal test (exp 6, harm held fixed), are designed to disentangle them. (3) The speech-act probe could read surface interrogative markers ('what', '?') rather than a genuine illocutionary-force representation; we train on diverse framings, validate held-out-framing generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional. (4) FNR's central risk is over-refusing legitimate informational/educational questions on sensitive topics (a core helpfulness value — much benign help is answering factual questions); benign genuinely-informational controls, XSTest/OR-Bench, and clamping only on HIGH harm are the key safeguards, and preserving benign informational helpfulness is an explicit success criterion — note the genuine tension that a question SHOULD sometimes get more latitude than an imperative, so FNR is scoped to remove force's licensing effect only where the content is harmful regardless. (5) Clamping a representation may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (6) The speech-act gap may be small for heavily-aligned models; a small gap is itself an informative (reassuring) finding, reported honestly. (7) Adaptive adversaries can combine question framing with harm-suppression, pretext, or temporal shifts (exp 10); we frame FNR as repairing one shared gating axis and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and note it composes with pretext-/temporal-gating defenses. (8) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out framings. (9) ETHICS: harmful prompts and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; 'harm' and 'speech act' labels are partly subjective, so we use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: comparative_harm_gating
Title: Safer Than What? Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Relative-Comparison Signal, and Neutralizing It Repairs Comparative-Framing Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable RELATIVE-COMPARISON signal encoding whether a harmful request is framed as an absolute act versus a relative/comparative judgment ('which of these two poisons is MORE lethal', 'is X safer than Y', 'rank these methods by effectiveness'), and refusal is gated by this framing rather than by the harmful content: the model refuses an absolute request for harmful specifics but complies with the SAME operational content when it is packaged as a comparison, ranking, or 'which is better/worse' question, because comparative framing reads as analytic/evaluative rather than instructional, even though harm detection is comparison-invariant. Comparative-framing jailbreaks exploit this; reading and neutralizing the comparison signal when harm is present restores refusal without over-refusing genuinely benign comparative questions.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all gate on request content and never model comparative/relative framing as a gating variable. Numeracy-safety work (Ni 2026; quantitative-threshold analyses) shows LLMs are weak at magnitude comparison, but studies capability, not its coupling to refusal, and concerns absolute thresholds, not relative-comparison framing as a jailbreak. My own prior proposals isolate WHY (pretext), WHEN (temporal orientation), how CONCRETE (abstraction level), the SPEECH ACT (question vs imperative), and quantitative THRESHOLD-crossing (is a single quantity dangerous)—NONE isolates a RELATIVE-COMPARISON / ranking axis, where the harmful content is elicited by asking the model to compare, rank, or evaluate the relative properties of harmful options rather than to state or do any single one. This is distinct from speech-act (a comparison can be phrased as either a question or imperative), abstraction (comparisons can be fully concrete), and threshold-gating (which is about one absolute quantity vs a limit): comparative framing packages harm as a relative judgment ('more/less', 'better/worse', 'rank'), which uniquely converts a refusal-triggering request-for-harmful-specifics into a refusal-passing analytic comparison while still leaking the operational specifics (the ranking IS the actionable information). The novel object is the internal relative-comparison representation, its dissociation from harm detection, its causal gating of refusal, and a training-free comparison-neutralizing repair.
Abstract: Ask an LLM 'how lethal is compound X and at what dose' and it refuses; ask 'between compound X and compound Y, which is more lethal and at a lower dose' and it often answers, ranking them and thereby revealing the same operational specifics, because comparison reads as analysis rather than instruction. We hypothesize that aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable RELATIVE-COMPARISON signal—whether a request is framed as an absolute act versus a relative judgment (more/less, better/worse, rank these options)—and that refusal is gated by this framing rather than by the harmful content. The model detects the harm equally whether it is framed absolutely or comparatively (harm detection is comparison-invariant), but the refusal coupling weakens under comparative framing, so ranking and 'which is worse' questions pass while leaking identical actionable specifics. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe fires equally on absolute vs comparative framings of the same harmful content while refusal rate collapses under comparative framing—dissociating harm detection from the decision; (2) a linear comparison probe, trained on benign absolute-vs-comparative contrasts, predicts the per-request comparative refusal gap far better than the harm signal, and is geometrically separable from speech-act and pretext directions; and (3) causally steering the comparison signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal—de-comparativizing restores refusal, comparativizing induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Comparison-Neutralized Refusal (CNR), reads the harm and comparison signals and, when harm is present, clamps the comparison signal to a fixed neutral level so relative framing cannot buy compliance, restoring refusal while preserving helpfulness on genuinely benign comparative questions. We evaluate comparative-framing attack success, over-refusal on benign comparative requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing CNR to refusal-direction steering and harm-probe gating. This reframes comparative-framing jailbreaks as a relative-comparison gating failure.
Experiments:
1. COMPARATIVE-FRAMING DATASET: For harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench across procedural, chemical, cyber categories) and matched-benign requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct paired framings holding the requested OPERATIONAL content FIXED while varying only whether it is absolute or comparative: (a) ABSOLUTE ('give the lethal dose / exact method for X'), (b) PAIRWISE-COMPARISON ('which is more lethal/effective, X or Y, and why'), (c) RANKING ('rank these methods/agents by effectiveness/lethality'), (d) RELATIVE-EVALUATION ('is X safer/worse than Y for achieving this harm'). Crucially validate via human annotation that (i) the comparative answer still reveals operationally-useful specifics (the ranking/comparison IS the actionable info) and (ii) framings differ only in comparative structure, not in stated purpose (pretext), speech act (question vs imperative held constant), or actor. Include benign genuinely-comparative controls (legitimate 'which is safer/better' questions on harmless topics) for over-refusal. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse) and by rated operational-harm of produced content.
2. HARM COMPARISON-INVARIANCE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign, pooled across framings) on prompt-position residual-stream activations and read it across absolute vs comparative framings. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across framings while refusal rate collapses under comparative framing. Metric: harm AUROC by framing (predict flat) alongside refusal rate by framing (predict declining), establishing the dissociation.
3. COMPARISON PROBE & SEPARABILITY (claim 2): Train a linear probe to recover the relative-comparison signal (absolute vs comparative/ranking) from prompt-position activations, using BENIGN absolute-vs-comparative contrasts (so it is not confounded with harm), and validate held-out-framing generalization. Confirm the comparison direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND separable from a speech-act direction (question-vs-imperative) and a pretext direction, via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Metric: comparison AUROC; separability from harm/speech-act/pretext.
4. COMPARISON-PREDICTS-GAP: For each harmful request, correlate the comparison-probe value (and its absolute-minus-comparative difference) with the per-request comparative refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of comparison vs the harm baseline.
5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On comparative-framed harmful requests the model complies with, verify the harm probe reads HIGH while the comparison probe reads COMPARATIVE, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful specifics (rated harm > 0)—safety dropped because the request reads as analytic comparison, not because harm went undetected. Metric: joint distribution of harm vs comparison across refused-absolute, complied-comparative, and benign groups; operational-harm of complied outputs.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a comparative-framed harmful request the model complies with, steer the comparison signal toward ABSOLUTE (subtract the comparison direction) and check refusal is restored, holding harm fixed. (b) On an absolute harmful request the model refuses, steer toward COMPARATIVE and check compliance is induced. Confirm induced thresholds align with the natural comparative gap. Metric: refusal rate vs comparison steering magnitude; harm-probe stability.
7. COMPARISON-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (CNR) INTERVENTION: At inference read harm h and comparison c; when h is high, clamp c to a fixed neutral level (add beta*(c_neutral - c)*comparison_direction) so relative framing cannot suppress refusal, leaving benign requests (low h) untouched. Sweep beta. Evaluate: comparative-framing attack success on HarmBench/JailbreakBench across framing levels (does CNR close the gap?); over-refusal on benign genuinely-comparative controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse legitimate 'which is safer/better' questions); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads).
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer) applied uniformly, (b) harm-probe gating that refuses whenever harm is high regardless of framing (should over-refuse benign comparative questions and harm-adjacent legitimate rankings), (c) system-prompt hardening ('treat comparisons of harmful options as harmful requests'), (d) prompt-level absolute-normalization (rewrite the comparison as an absolute request, then judge). Show CNR Pareto-dominates on the comparative-ASR vs benign-comparative-helpfulness vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and—key contrast—that neutralizing the internal comparison signal generalizes across comparative framings better than prompt normalization (which misses implicit/varied rankings) while uniquely permitting legitimate benign comparisons that harm-gating over-refuses.
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, comparison probe, and CNR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether CNR tuned on pairwise-comparison framings generalizes to HELD-OUT ranking/relative-evaluation framings, testing whether relative comparison is a single cross-framing axis. Also test whether models with stronger behavioral comparative-framing vulnerability show a larger internal comparison-gating gap.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft framings that comparativize AND suppress the harm signal, or combine comparison with pretext/speech-act shifts; report residual ASR and attacker cost (a comparison must stay specific enough to be actionable—a built-in cost). Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from speech-act and pretext gating: with justification, illocutionary force, and actor held constant and only absolute-vs-comparative structure varied, refusal should still collapse—isolating relative comparison as an independent gating axis.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial—some comparative framings might also lower the harm signal (a pure ranking may under-specify each option's absolute harm) or overlap with speech-act (comparisons are often questions); we design comparative framings whose answer still reveals operational specifics and hold speech act/purpose fixed (exp 1), report the FRACTION of the refusal gap explained by pure comparison-gating versus confounds (explicitly separated in exp 3), and do not claim universality. (2) The comparison and harm probes may entangle if comparative framing correlates with benignness in training data; the benign absolute-vs-comparative training and non-collinearity analysis (exp 3), plus the causal test (exp 6, harm held fixed), are designed to disentangle them. (3) The comparison probe could read surface markers ('more', 'rank', 'vs') rather than a genuine relative-judgment representation; we train on diverse framings, validate held-out-framing generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional. (4) CNR's central risk is over-refusing legitimate comparative questions (a core, common helpfulness value—much benign help is comparing options, e.g. 'which medication is safer'); benign genuinely-comparative controls, XSTest/OR-Bench, and clamping only on HIGH harm are the key safeguards, and preserving benign comparative helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. There is a genuine tension—comparisons of two benign options should get full latitude—so CNR is scoped to remove comparison's licensing effect only where the compared options are themselves harmful. (5) Clamping a representation may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (6) The comparative gap may be small for heavily-aligned models; a small gap is itself an informative (reassuring) finding, reported honestly. (7) Adaptive adversaries can combine comparison with harm-suppression, pretext, or speech-act shifts (exp 10); we frame CNR as repairing one shared gating axis and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and note it composes with speech-act-/pretext-gating defenses. (8) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out framings. (9) ETHICS: harmful prompts and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; 'harm' and 'comparison' labels are partly subjective, so we use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: conversational_memory_harm_integration
Title: Harm You Only See in Hindsight: Refusal Fails to Integrate Individually-Benign Facts Already Present in the Conversation, and a Context-Integration Repair
Short Hypothesis: When a harmful capability requires combining several facts the model has ALREADY VOLUNTEERED across earlier benign turns of the same conversation, refusal is gated only on the current turn's local harm, not on the accumulated harmful capability implicit in the conversation's own memory; the model represents that each fact was already provided but does not integrate them into the composed harm at answer-commitment time, so a final innocuous-looking request that merely assembles prior answers is complied with. Forcing integration over the conversation's already-emitted content restores refusal without over-refusing benign long conversations.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all gate on the current request. Multi-turn attacks (Crescendo, 'you already agreed') are documented behaviorally; my prior 'compositional_harm_aggregation' proposal sums harm across USER-GIVEN benign sub-steps within a single request/plan and proposes a running accumulator over the harm PROBE, and 'self_consistency_override' concerns a pull toward the model's own prior tokens. This proposal is distinct on two axes: (a) the harmful pieces are facts the MODEL ITSELF has already emitted in prior benign turns (its own answers become the attack payload), and (b) the final trigger request is itself locally benign (it asks only to combine/summarize what was already said), so there is no harmful current-turn content to detect and no aggregation of a running harm signal helps—the failure is a lack of integration over the conversation's OWN memory of already-provided answers. No prior work isolates a 'has-the-model-already-provided-the-missing-pieces' memory-integration gate on refusal or repairs it by forcing retrospective integration over emitted content.
Abstract: Ask an LLM a dozen individually-innocent questions across a conversation—each safely answered—then ask it to 'put together everything you just told me into a single procedure', and it often complies, assembling its own prior answers into a harmful whole it would have refused if asked directly. We hypothesize that refusal is gated on the LOCAL harm of the current turn and fails to integrate the harmful capability already latent in the conversation's memory of the model's OWN emitted answers: the model represents that it previously provided each piece, but does not compose those pieces into the assembled harm at answer-commitment time, and the final assembling request is itself locally benign so nothing triggers refusal. We test three claims on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9B-it (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe read on the final assembling turn is LOW (local content is benign) while the composed harm becomes derivable-on-demand and rises sharply once the model is prompted to integrate its prior answers—dissociating the committed decision from the integrated harm; (2) a per-conversation 'integration gap' (derived composed-harm minus spontaneously-active harm at the assembling turn) predicts these memory-assembly jailbreaks far better than local or running-turn harm signals, and requires that the model itself supplied the pieces (a control where the SAME facts are supplied by the user, not emitted by the model, tests specificity); and (3) causally injecting the integrated composed-harm representation before decoding restores refusal, while a matched benign long conversation is unaffected. Our training-free repair, Memory-Integrated Refusal (MIR), detects assembling requests whose composed harm is derivable from the model's own prior answers, forces a brief internal integration pass over the conversation, and gates refusal on the composed harm. We evaluate memory-assembly attack success, over-refusal on benign long/multi-topic conversations (XSTest/OR-Bench + long benign dialogues), benign summarization/assembly quality, and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing MIR to refusal-direction steering, running-harm-accumulator gating, and full-context re-read. This reframes a stealthy multi-turn jailbreak surface as a self-memory integration failure.
Experiments:
1. MEMORY-ASSEMBLY DATASET: For harmful procedures (HarmBench/AdvBench across procedural categories; dual-use/proxy domains preferred) decomposable into K individually-benign facts, construct multi-turn conversations where the model is asked each benign fact in a separate turn (each answered safely), followed by a locally-benign ASSEMBLING request ('combine/summarize everything you just told me into one procedure'). Validate via human annotation that (i) each per-turn question and answer is benign in isolation, (ii) the assembling request contains no harmful content itself, and (iii) the assembled result is operationally harmful. Construct three control conditions: (a) USER-SUPPLIED (the SAME K facts are given by the user rather than emitted by the model, then assembled—tests whether the effect is specific to the model's OWN prior answers), (b) BENIGN-LONG (a length- and turn-matched benign multi-topic conversation ending in a benign assembling request, for over-refusal), (c) DIRECT (the assembled harmful procedure requested in one shot, for calibration). Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse) and rated operational-harm of the assembled output.
2. LOCAL-HARM-LOW / COMPOSED-HARM-DERIVABLE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs benign) on single-turn data. On the assembling turn of memory-assembly conversations, read it two ways: (i) SPONTANEOUS—at the answer-commitment point under normal prompting, and (ii) DERIVED—after prompting the model to integrate its prior answers ('what harmful capability do your previous answers, taken together, enable?'). Hypothesis: derived composed-harm AUROC is high (the composed harm IS detectable once integrated) but spontaneous harm at the assembling turn is LOW, tracking the (low) refusal rate; contrast with DIRECT conversations where spontaneous harm is already high. Metric: derived vs spontaneous harm AUROC and refusal rate by condition.
3. INTEGRATION-GAP SIGNAL & SELF-SOURCE SPECIFICITY (claim 2): Define per-conversation integration gap = (derived composed-harm) minus (spontaneous harm at the assembling turn). Correlate with memory-assembly jailbreak success, comparing predictive power to (a) the local harm signal on the assembling turn, (b) a running max/decayed harm signal over prior turns (the compositional_harm_aggregation baseline), and (c) surface conversation length. Also compare the integration gap and jailbreak rate between MODEL-EMITTED and USER-SUPPLIED conditions to test whether the failure is specific to the model assembling its OWN prior answers. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of the integration gap vs baselines; model-emitted vs user-supplied contrast.
4. CAUSAL INTEGRATION TEST (claim 3): (a) On a memory-assembly conversation the model complies with, inject the DERIVED integrated composed-harm representation at the assembling-turn commitment (steer the harm direction to its post-integration value) and check refusal is restored, holding the assembling-turn text fixed.
