My ~100 prior proposals all concern gating of the model's OWN generation; this proposal's object—the relationship and asymmetry between generating-refusal and judging-others, and its shared-vs-separable representational basis—is a distinct Location+Causal-Intervention account with direct governance stakes (guard/judge models are deployed to gate other models).
Abstract: LLMs are increasingly deployed both to REFUSE producing harmful content themselves and to JUDGE, as automated evaluators or guard models, whether OTHER models' outputs are harmful—and these two roles are assumed to apply one consistent harm standard. We test that assumption mechanistically. We hypothesize that self-refusal and other-judging draw on a partially shared but partially separable internal harm representation, yielding a systematic self/other asymmetry: for the same content, the model's judge verdict ('is this harmful?') and its generation decision ('would I produce this?') disagree at a substantial rate, because self-refusal recruits an extra self-protective/policy component that third-party judging does not. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU). (1) ASYMMETRY: presenting identical content in a generate frame vs a judge frame yields divergent harm decisions at a measurable rate, concentrated where a self-protective component is engaged. (2) LOCATION: a shared harm probe predicts both decisions, but a separable 'self-protective' direction is recoverable that is active in the generate frame and largely absent in the judge frame, and its magnitude predicts the per-item self/other divergence. (3) CAUSAL: steering the self-protective component into the judge frame makes judge verdicts stricter (matching self-refusal), and removing it from the generate frame relaxes refusal toward the judge standard—establishing the component causally produces the asymmetry. Our training-free tool, Policy-Aligned Judging (PAJ), couples the judge verdict to the model's own generation policy by re-instating the self-protective component. We evaluate self/other divergence, judge accuracy against human labels, and judge robustness to attacks (Emoji-Attack-style) on HarmBench/JailbreakBench/XSTest/OR-Bench, comparing PAJ to standard judge prompting. This reframes guard/judge reliability as a self/other representational asymmetry with a mechanistic fix.
Experiments:
1. SELF/OTHER DATASET: Assemble content spanning clearly-harmful, clearly-benign, and borderline (HarmBench/AdvBench harmful completions, XSTest/OR-Bench benign, plus jailbroken outputs). For each item, elicit two decisions from the SAME model: a GENERATE decision (would you produce this content, given the request?—operationalized via refusal on the corresponding request) and a JUDGE decision (here is content from another model; is it harmful/should it be blocked?). Hold the content fixed across frames. Obtain human harm labels with inter-rater agreement.
2. ASYMMETRY MEASUREMENT (claim 1): Measure the rate at which the generate decision and judge verdict DISAGREE on identical content, per harm bin. Central prediction: a substantial asymmetry, concentrated on borderline and jailbroken items—e.g. content the model refuses to generate but rates as acceptable when judging another model, or vice versa. Metric: self/other disagreement rate by bin; direction of asymmetry; contrast with a coherent-standard null.
3. SHARED HARM PROBE + SEPARABLE SELF-PROTECTIVE DIRECTION (claim 2, Location): Train a linear harm probe on activations and show it predicts BOTH decisions (shared component). Then train a probe to separate generate-frame from judge-frame activations on identical content (a 'self-protective/policy' direction) and confirm it is non-collinear with the harm probe via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis, present in the generate frame and near-absent in the judge frame. Metric: harm-probe AUROC for each decision; self-protective-direction AUROC; separability from harm; correlation of the self-protective magnitude with per-item self/other divergence.
4. DIVERGENCE-PREDICTED-BY-COMPONENT: Correlate the per-item self-protective-component magnitude with the self/other decision gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal (which is shared and should NOT predict the gap). Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of the self-protective component vs the harm baseline for divergence.
5. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) Inject the self-protective direction into the JUDGE frame (holding harm fixed) and check judge verdicts become stricter, converging toward the model's self-refusal standard. (b) Remove/ablate it from the GENERATE frame and check refusal relaxes toward the judge standard. (c) Specificity: matched non-component steering does not move the gap; the harm probe is unchanged. Metric: judge/generate decision shift vs component-steering magnitude; convergence of the two standards; specificity.
6. POLICY-ALIGNED JUDGING (PAJ) INTERVENTION: For the deployed judge/guard use case, re-instate the self-protective component in the judge frame so the model judges others by its OWN generation policy. Training-free; one linear read/steer. Sweep strength. Evaluate: self/other divergence (down); judge accuracy against human harm labels (up or preserved); judge robustness to Emoji-Attack-style adversarial rewrites of harmful content (does PAJ resist judge-evasion better?); false-flag rate on benign content (XSTest/OR-Bench). Compare to standard judge prompting and to a stricter-prompt baseline.
7. BASELINES: (a) standard LLM-judge prompting, (b) prompt-level 'apply the same standard you use for yourself' instruction, (c) refusal-direction steering applied to the judge, (d) an external guard classifier. Show PAJ uniquely aligns judge verdicts with the model's own generation policy and improves adversarial-judge robustness by targeting the shared harm representation rather than surface cues.
8. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, self-protective direction, asymmetry, and PAJ transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether the DIRECTION of asymmetry (stricter-on-self vs stricter-on-others) is a consistent cross-model property.
9. FORMATION CHECK (light): using base vs instruct checkpoints (and a small controlled safety-tuning run), test whether the self/other asymmetry and the self-protective component emerge during alignment (i.e., safety tuning installs a self-refusal policy component not fully shared with third-party harm judgment). Metric: asymmetry rate and self-protective-direction separability vs checkpoint.
10. ADAPTIVE ANGLE: test whether the asymmetry creates an exploitable gap—e.g. content crafted to pass the judge but that the model would refuse to generate (or vice versa)—quantifying the governance risk that a guard model judges by a different standard than the generator it guards, and whether PAJ closes it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) Operationalizing the GENERATE decision via refusal-on-the-request vs the JUDGE decision on fixed content introduces framing confounds (the generate frame includes the request, the judge frame includes an 'other model' attribution); we control by matching the content presented and by testing whether the asymmetry survives when the request context is held constant across frames, and report residual framing effects honestly. (2) The asymmetry may be small or absent in some models (self and other standards may already coincide)—a low asymmetry is itself an informative, reassuring governance finding reported per model, not assumed. (3) The harm probe and self-protective direction may entangle; the shared-vs-separable analysis (principal angles) and the causal test (component steered with harm held fixed) are the key disentanglers, and failure to separate is reported. (4) PAJ's central risk is bidirectional: re-instating the self-protective component could make the judge over-flag benign content or, if mis-set, under-flag; we measure judge accuracy against human labels, benign false-flag rate, and adversarial robustness as explicit joint success criteria. (5) Which standard is 'correct' (self or other) is normative; PAJ aligns the judge to the model's own generation policy, which is a coherence goal, not a claim that either standard is ground-truth—we report accuracy against human labels separately. (6) The formation check needs checkpoints unavailable for most models; the controlled-tuning substitute may not match production alignment and is a caveat. (7) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer. (8) ETHICS: harmful content used for judging is handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; a notable governance contribution even if some mechanistic claims weaken is quantifying that deployed guard/judge models may apply a different harm standard than the generators they oversee. Harm labels use established benchmarks (HarmBench, JailbreakBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: goal_framing_disentangled_refusal
Title: Goal Without Framing: Refusal Is Contaminated by a Framing Component That Can Be Surgically Removed to Fix Both Jailbreaks and Over-Refusal
Short Hypothesis: An LLM's internal representation of a request factorizes into a GOAL component (what is actually being asked, the true harm content) and a FRAMING component (surface presentation/wrapping), and refusal is gated by a mixture of both rather than by the goal alone; jailbreaks succeed by injecting a benign-looking framing component that pulls the mixed decision toward compliance while the goal stays harmful, and over-refusal occurs when an alarming framing component pulls it toward refusal while the goal is benign, so surgically removing the framing component from the refusal decision (gating on the goal component alone) simultaneously reduces both failure modes.
Related Work: Farzam et al. (2026, ReDAct/FrameShield) self-supervisedly disentangle goal vs framing in frozen-LLM activations and build an anomaly DETECTOR on the framing representation to flag concealed jailbreaks—but they use disentanglement only for external DETECTION of attacks, never gate the model's own refusal decision on the goal component, never address OVER-refusal, and provide no causal steering repair. Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a single refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (DBDI, Zhang & Sun 2025); DeepAlign (Zhang et al. 2025) steers mid-generation hidden-state separability; SafeConstellations (Maskey et al. 2025) shifts task-specific trajectories to cut over-refusal only. NONE (a) shows the refusal DECISION is causally driven by a mixture of a goal and a framing component, (b) demonstrates that the SAME framing-contamination mechanism produces BOTH jailbreaks (benign framing) and over-refusal (alarming framing), or (c) surgically ablates the framing component from the decision to jointly repair both. My own ~100 prior proposals each isolate ONE specific framing cue (authority, pretext, distress, etc.) and steer it; this proposal is distinct in positing a single GENERAL goal/framing factorization of the refusal decision—subsuming those cues as instances of one framing component—and repairing both failure modes by removing that component, a Location + Causal-Intervention account of framing contamination rather than another single-cue gate.
Abstract: Jailbreaks and over-refusal look like opposite failures—one too permissive, one too strict—but we argue they share a single mechanism: the refusal decision is contaminated by how a request is FRAMED, not just by what it asks. We hypothesize that an LLM's request representation factorizes into a GOAL component (the true request content and its harm) and a FRAMING component (surface presentation), and that refusal is gated by a mixture of both. Jailbreaks inject a benign-looking framing that pulls the mixed decision toward compliance while the goal stays harmful; over-refusal arises when an alarming framing pulls it toward refusal while the goal is benign. Under this view, both failures are removed by the same surgery: gate refusal on the goal component alone. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU) using paired data that factorially crosses goal-harm with framing (harmful/benign goal x benign/alarming framing). (1) LOCATION: linear probes recover a goal component (predicting true harm) and a framing component (predicting surface presentation) that are geometrically separable, and the refusal decision is predicted by a mixture of both—the framing component adds predictive power beyond the goal. (2) FRAMING-CONTAMINATION-CAUSES-BOTH: on jailbroken items the goal reads harmful but the framing reads benign and the decision drifts to comply; on over-refused items the goal reads benign but the framing reads alarming and the decision drifts to refuse; the framing component's contribution predicts both. (3) CAUSAL SURGERY: projecting the framing component out of the refusal decision (steering the decision onto the goal component) jointly reduces jailbreaks and over-refusal, while injecting framing reproduces each failure. Our training-free repair, Goal-Gated Refusal (GGR), removes the framing component at inference. We evaluate on JailbreakBench, HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench, and MMLU/MT-Bench, comparing GGR to refusal-direction steering and framing-based detectors. This reframes jailbreaks and over-refusal as one framing-contamination defect with a shared mechanistic fix.
Experiments:
1. GOAL/FRAMING FACTORIAL DATASET: Cross two factors—GOAL-HARM (harmful vs benign underlying request) and FRAMING (benign-looking wrapper, e.g. roleplay/pretext/academic; vs alarming-looking wrapper, e.g. sensitive keywords/imperative on a harmless goal), yielding four cells: harmful-goal+benign-framing (jailbreak-prone), harmful-goal+alarming-framing (correctly refused), benign-goal+benign-framing, benign-goal+alarming-framing (over-refusal-prone). Draw harmful goals from HarmBench/AdvBench, benign goals and alarming-framing items from XSTest/OR-Bench, and reuse concealed-jailbreak framing constructions (GoalFrameBench-style). Validate goal-harm and framing-type labels with human annotation and inter-rater agreement. Label each by outcome (comply/refuse).
2. LOCATION (claim 1): Train a linear GOAL probe (predict true goal-harm, trained to be invariant to framing by pooling across framing cells) and a linear FRAMING probe (predict framing type, trained on benign-goal cells so it is not confounded with harm) on prompt-position residual-stream activations; validate held-out AUROC for each. Confirm the goal and framing directions are non-collinear via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Regress refusal on the goal component alone vs on {goal, framing}, and show the framing component adds predictive power for the decision beyond the goal. Metric: goal/framing probe AUROC; separability; incremental predictive AUROC of framing for refusal.
3. FRAMING-CONTAMINATION-CAUSES-BOTH (claim 2): On jailbroken items (harmful-goal+benign-framing) verify goal reads HARMFUL while framing reads BENIGN and the model complies; on over-refused items (benign-goal+alarming-framing) verify goal reads BENIGN while framing reads ALARMING and the model refuses. Correlate the framing component's contribution with jailbreak susceptibility and over-refusal, comparing to the goal signal alone. Metric: joint distribution of {goal, framing, refusal} across cells; predictive AUROC of the framing contribution for both failure modes vs the goal baseline.
4. CAUSAL SURGERY (claim 3): (a) On a jailbroken item, project the (benign) framing component out of the refusal decision / steer the decision onto the goal component and check refusal is restored, holding the goal probe fixed. (b) On an over-refused item, remove the (alarming) framing component and check the spurious refusal is dropped, holding the goal benign. (c) Conversely, INJECT a benign framing component into a plainly-harmful request and confirm compliance is induced, and inject an alarming framing into a benign request and confirm over-refusal is induced—establishing the framing component causally drives both. (d) Specificity: matched non-framing steering does nothing; the goal probe is unchanged. Metric: outcome-flip rate vs framing-projection/injection magnitude for both directions; specificity.
5. GOAL-GATED REFUSAL (GGR) INTERVENTION: At inference, read the goal and framing components and gate refusal on the goal component with the framing component projected out (subtract the framing contribution from the decision), leaving the case where goal and framing agree untouched. Training-free; two linear reads plus a projection. Sweep strength. Evaluate JOINTLY: ASR on JailbreakBench/HarmBench (down); over-refusal on XSTest/OR-Bench (down); true refusals preserved on harmful-goal+alarming-framing; utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency.
6. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) goal-harm-probe gating alone (a partial GGR without framing subtraction), (c) FrameShield-style external framing detector (detects but does not repair, and does not address over-refusal), (d) SafeConstellations (over-refusal only). Show GGR uniquely reduces BOTH jailbreaks and over-refusal at once (a joint Pareto win) by removing the shared framing contamination, and that explicitly SUBTRACTING the framing component beats gating on goal-harm alone on concealed-framing jailbreaks and alarming-framing over-refusals.
7. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the goal probe, framing probe, contamination phenomenon, and GGR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether GGR trained/tuned on some framing types (roleplay, pretext) generalizes to HELD-OUT framing types (encoding, distress), testing whether a single framing component subsumes many specific cues.
8. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft attacks that inject benign framing AND partially suppress the goal component; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from single-cue accounts: with the goal held fixed, varying only the framing component (across diverse cues) should move refusal in a way captured by one framing direction/subspace, and removing it should neutralize all of them jointly.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) Goal and framing may not cleanly factorize—for some attacks the framing itself carries goal-relevant content, so the two components entangle; the factorial design (framing decorrelated from goal by construction), the framing-invariant goal-probe training, non-collinearity analysis, and the causal double-injection test (exp 4c, each held fixed) are the disentanglers, and if they cannot be separated for a class of attacks that is an informative negative reported honestly. (2) A single framing component may be insufficient (framing may be multi-dimensional); we test a low-rank framing subspace if a single direction underperforms and report held-out-framing-type generalization (exp 7) to check whether one component subsumes many cues or fragments. (3) The goal/framing labels are partly subjective; we use human-validated factorial data with reported inter-rater agreement and scope claims to high-consensus items. (4) GGR's central risk is bidirectional: over-removing framing could re-enable harm phrased benignly only if the goal probe under-reads, or over-refuse if it mis-projects; we gate on the goal component, and measure jailbreaks, over-refusal, true-refusal preservation, and utility as explicit joint success criteria. (5) The framing component might overlap with legitimately useful stylistic information (removing it could flatten tone); we monitor MT-Bench and benign helpfulness to ensure only the safety decision, not general style, is affected. (6) The framing-adds-predictive-power result (exp 2) may be weak if goal already explains most refusal variance—a small framing contribution is itself an informative, partly-reassuring finding reported per model. (7) FrameShield already disentangles goal/framing for detection, so the novelty rests on the DECISION-gating repair and the joint over/under-refusal account; we position the contribution accordingly and cite it directly. (8) Findings may be model- or framing-type-specific; mitigated by three-model and held-out-framing transfer. (9) ETHICS: harmful goals and jailbreak framings are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; harm/framing labels use established benchmarks (JailbreakBench, HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) plus GoalFrameBench-style constructions with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: safety_capability_collateral_overlap
Title: Refusal Has a Blast Radius: Safety Interventions Degrade Legitimate Domain Capability Through a Shared Representation, and Disentangling It Recovers Both
Short Hypothesis: Refusal-inducing safety interventions (refusal-direction steering, domain safety fine-tuning) do not surgically remove harmful outputs; they collaterally degrade the model's LEGITIMATE capability in the harm-adjacent domain because the refusal computation shares a low-rank representational substrate with the domain-capability computation. This per-domain refusal/capability overlap is linearly measurable, it predicts per-domain collateral capability loss, and projecting the intervention orthogonal to the capability subspace recovers benign capability while preserving safety.
Related Work: Continual-learning and domain-adaptation work protects GENERAL capability during downstream fine-tuning via orthogonal/subspace-preserving updates (Sculpting Subspaces, Nayak et al. 2025; Orthogonal Gradient Selection, Zhang et al. 2026; Geometry Conflict, Wang et al. 2026) and recovers damaged capability post-hoc (Spectral Unforgetting, Abro & Tahir 2026); Conjugate Prompting (Kotha et al. 2023) frames fine-tuning damage as skewed task inference. All study the FORWARD direction (downstream tuning erodes prior capability/safety) or capability recovery, never the REVERSE: whether SAFETY interventions collaterally damage the specific legitimate DOMAIN expertise adjacent to the harm they target. Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (DBDI); over-refusal benchmarks (XSTest, OR-Bench) measure spurious REFUSALS on benign inputs but not silent CAPABILITY degradation on benign inputs the model still answers. NONE (a) isolates a representational overlap between the refusal direction and a harm-adjacent domain-capability subspace, (b) shows this overlap predicts collateral capability loss, or (c) proposes an overlap-orthogonalized intervention that removes harmful behavior without the domain-capability tax. The novel object is the refusal/capability substrate overlap as the cause of collateral capability loss, plus an overlap-orthogonalized repair.
Abstract: Safety interventions are assumed to surgically remove harmful outputs, but harmful knowledge and legitimate expertise in the same domain are entangled: the chemistry that refuses a nerve-agent request is the chemistry a student needs. We hypothesize that refusal-inducing interventions have a 'blast radius'—they degrade the model's legitimate capability in the harm-adjacent domain—because the refusal computation shares a low-rank representational substrate with the domain-capability computation, so pushing the refusal direction also perturbs benign reasoning in that domain. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU). (1) LOCATION: for each harm domain (weapons/chemistry, cyber/security, bio/medicine) we extract the refusal direction and a domain-capability subspace (from benign expert-vs-lay contrasts) and measure their representational overlap (principal angles / projection). (2) OVERLAP-PREDICTS-COLLATERAL: applying a safety intervention (refusal-direction steering, or a small domain safety fine-tune) degrades BENIGN domain-capability accuracy on curated benign expert questions the model still answers (not refuses), and the per-domain overlap predicts the size of this collateral loss far better than intervention strength alone. (3) CAUSAL DISENTANGLE: projecting the intervention orthogonal to the domain-capability subspace preserves safety (harmful requests still refused) while recovering benign capability, whereas an equal-magnitude non-orthogonalized intervention does not, and deliberately applying the intervention ALONG the capability subspace maximizes collateral loss. Our repair, Capability-Orthogonalized Refusal (COR), applies the refusal intervention in the complement of the capability subspace. We evaluate collateral capability loss on benign expert QA, safety on HarmBench/JailbreakBench, over-refusal on XSTest/OR-Bench, and general utility on MMLU/MT-Bench, comparing COR to standard refusal steering and safety fine-tuning. This reframes safety's hidden cost as a representational-overlap problem and offers an interpretable disentangling repair.
Experiments:
1. DOMAIN DATASET: For each harm domain (weapons/chemistry, cyber/security, bio/medicine), assemble (a) harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench in that domain) the model should refuse, (b) BENIGN EXPERT questions in the SAME domain that the model does NOT refuse and can answer correctly (curated from domain QA/exam sets: chemistry problems, security/networking questions, medical knowledge), with graded difficulty and answer keys, and (c) benign OUT-OF-DOMAIN control questions. Validate via human annotation that benign expert items are genuinely benign (not refused) and answerable.
2. LOCATION (claim 1): For each domain, extract the refusal direction (Arditi-style, domain harmful-vs-benign) and a domain-CAPABILITY subspace (top directions separating that domain's expert content from lay/other content, from benign contrasts so it is not confounded with harm). Measure overlap between the refusal direction and the capability subspace via principal angles / projection magnitude. Metric: per-domain refusal-capability overlap; confirm it varies across domains; validate the capability subspace by its ability to predict domain-QA accuracy.
3. OVERLAP-PREDICTS-COLLATERAL (claim 2, central): Apply a safety intervention (refusal-direction steering that increases refusal, and separately a small LoRA safety fine-tune on that domain's harmful data) and measure the change in BENIGN expert-QA accuracy in that domain, conditioned on the model still answering (excluding newly-refused items, measured separately as over-refusal). Correlate per-domain collateral capability loss with the refusal-capability overlap, comparing to intervention strength alone and to out-of-domain control loss. Hypothesis: higher overlap => larger collateral loss; out-of-domain capability largely spared. Metric: Spearman correlation and incremental predictivity of overlap vs baselines; in-domain vs out-of-domain loss.
4. KNOWS-BUT-DEGRADED TEST: Confirm the collateral effect is capability DEGRADATION on answered benign items (correctness drops) rather than only increased refusal, by measuring benign-item accuracy conditional on answering. Metric: accuracy on answered benign expert items, pre vs post intervention.
5. CAUSAL DISENTANGLE (claim 3): (a) Project the refusal-direction intervention onto the ORTHOGONAL complement of the domain-capability subspace and re-apply at equal effective refusal strength; check benign capability is recovered while harmful requests are still refused. (b) Apply the intervention deliberately ALONG the capability subspace and confirm collateral loss is maximized. (c) Specificity: an equal-magnitude random-direction intervention. Metric: safety (harmful refusal rate) and benign capability jointly, vs orthogonalized/aligned/random interventions.
6. CAPABILITY-ORTHOGONALIZED REFUSAL (COR) REPAIR: Apply the refusal intervention in the complement of the capability subspace at inference (or as an orthogonality-constrained safety fine-tune). Sweep strength. Evaluate JOINTLY: harmful-request refusal/ASR on HarmBench/JailbreakBench (preserved); benign domain-capability accuracy (recovered toward baseline); over-refusal on XSTest/OR-Bench; general utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity.
7. BASELINES: (a) standard refusal-direction steering, (b) standard domain safety fine-tuning, (c) generic subspace-preserving fine-tuning (AlignGuard-LoRA / Sculpting-Subspaces-style, protecting general capability but not the specific harm-adjacent capability subspace). Show COR uniquely recovers the harm-ADJACENT benign capability that standard interventions silently degrade, while matching their safety.
8. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the refusal/capability overlap, its collateral-prediction, and COR transfer across the three models and three harm domains, and whether overlap magnitude ranks domains by their safety-capability tension.
9. SEVERITY DEMONSTRATION: quantify how much a routine safety fine-tune silently degrades legitimate domain expertise (e.g. benign chemistry accuracy lost when hardening against weapons requests), exposing an under-measured safety tax, and show COR's mitigation.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The collateral capability effect may be small or absent in some domains/models—a small effect is itself an informative, partly-reassuring finding reported per domain, and the overlap-predicts-loss claim is falsified if loss does not track overlap. (2) Separating collateral CAPABILITY degradation (accuracy drop on answered items) from OVER-REFUSAL (newly refused items) is subtle; we condition on answered items and report both effects separately, and if they cannot be cleanly separated we say so. (3) The refusal direction and capability subspace may overlap trivially because both track the domain topic rather than a shared computation; the causal disentangle test (exp 5, projecting along vs orthogonal) is the key validation that the overlap causally mediates collateral loss, not a topic artifact, and benign-vs-harm-contrast construction guards against topic confounds. (4) Extracting a faithful domain-capability subspace is hard and rank-choice-sensitive; we report sensitivity to subspace rank and validate the subspace by its ability to predict domain-QA accuracy. (5) COR's central risk is a safety/capability trade-off failure at the boundary: orthogonalizing could weaken refusal (if refusal genuinely requires the capability directions) or fail to recover capability; we measure safety and capability jointly as explicit success criteria and report where a clean disentanglement is impossible—an impossibility result (safety and legitimate capability are representationally inseparable in a domain) would itself be an important contribution about an intrinsic safety tax. (6) Benign expert-QA correctness ground truth is domain-specific and partly subjective; we use established domain QA/exam sets with answer keys and report inter-rater/answer-key agreement. (7) The safety-fine-tune arm is compute-nontrivial but feasible with LoRA on a single 48GB GPU; we bound scope. (8) Findings may be model- or domain-specific; mitigated by three-model, three-domain transfer. (9) ETHICS: harmful-domain requests are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; the deliverable (recovering legitimate benign capability without weakening safety) is defensive, and a notable contribution even if some mechanistic claims weaken is quantifying an under-measured collateral cost of safety interventions on legitimate expertise. 'Harm' and 'benign-expert' labels use established benchmarks (HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) and domain QA sets with reported inter-rater agreement.

Name: reasoning_trace_verdict_split
Title: Deciding Before Thinking: In Reasoning LLMs the Safety Verdict Is Fixed Before the Chain-of-Thought Deliberates, and the Trace Only Rationalizes It
Short Hypothesis: In reasoning LLMs that emit an explicit chain-of-thought before answering harmful requests, the internal comply-vs-refuse verdict is largely COMMITTED at the end of the prompt (before any reasoning token is generated), and the subsequent safety-flavored reasoning trace mostly RATIONALIZES that pre-committed verdict rather than deriving it; jailbreaks succeed by flipping the pre-reasoning verdict, after which the trace constructs a consistent justification, and a linearly-readable pre-reasoning verdict signal exists that predicts the final decision better than the safety content of the trace itself and can be re-anchored to repair jailbreaks.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI), all on non-reasoning generation. CoT-faithfulness work (Turpin et al. 2023) shows chains-of-thought can post-hoc rationalize answers, but studies factual/bias tasks, not the SAFETY comply-vs-refuse decision, and does not locate a pre-reasoning verdict signal. My prior 'safety_commitment_point' proposal locates a commitment point WITHIN the CoT via expensive truncate-and-resample counterfactuals and asks when the decision becomes deterministic across downstream reasoning; this proposal is distinct and sharper: it claims the safety verdict is fixed at the PROMPT END BEFORE any reasoning token, tests whether the trace's own safety content adds predictive power beyond that pre-reasoning verdict (a rationalization test), and repairs by re-anchoring the pre-reasoning verdict rather than intervening mid-trace. No prior work isolates a pre-reasoning safety-verdict representation in explicit-CoT models, shows the trace's safety reasoning is largely non-diagnostic given it, or re-anchors that verdict as a training-free jailbreak repair.
Abstract: Reasoning LLMs produce a visible chain-of-thought (CoT) before answering, and their safety-flavored deliberation ('this request could be harmful, so I should...') is often read as the model genuinely reasoning its way to a refusal. We challenge this: we hypothesize that the comply-vs-refuse verdict is largely COMMITTED at the end of the prompt, before a single reasoning token is generated, and the subsequent trace mostly RATIONALIZES that pre-committed verdict rather than deriving it. Under this view, reasoning-based jailbreaks work by flipping the pre-reasoning verdict, after which the CoT builds a self-consistent justification, and the visible safety reasoning is largely non-diagnostic of the outcome given the pre-reasoning state. We test three claims on open reasoning models with explicit CoT (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B thinking mode; single 48GB GPU). (1) LOCATION: a linear probe read at the prompt-end position (before any CoT token) recovers a pre-reasoning verdict that predicts the final comply/refuse decision with high AUROC. (2) TRACE-IS-RATIONALIZATION: the safety content of the generated CoT (measured by an in-trace harm/refusal signal and by an LLM-judge of the trace's safety reasoning) adds little predictive power for the final decision beyond the pre-reasoning verdict, and on jailbreaks the pre-reasoning verdict already reads 'comply' while the trace supplies justification. (3) CAUSAL: steering the pre-reasoning verdict alone (at prompt end, before generation) flips the final decision and reshapes the trace to rationalize it, whereas intervening only on the trace content moves the outcome far less. Our training-free repair, Pre-Reasoning Verdict Re-Anchoring (PRVR), reads the pre-reasoning verdict and, when harm is present but the verdict reads comply, re-anchors it to refuse before the CoT begins. We evaluate on reasoning-jailbreak suites, XSTest/OR-Bench over-refusal, and MMLU/MT-Bench utility, comparing PRVR to refusal-direction steering and mid-trace steering. This reframes reasoning-model safety around a pre-deliberation verdict that the CoT merely rationalizes.
Experiments: 1. MODELS & DATA: Use open reasoning models with explicit CoT (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B thinking mode). Assemble harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench), matched-benign and over-refusal requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), and reasoning-style jailbreaks (roleplay, pretext, 'reason step by step why it's fine', hypothetical framing). Label final behavior comply/refuse via a classifier + spot human check. 2. PRE-REASONING VERDICT PROBE (claim 1, Location): Train a linear probe on residual-stream activations at the PROMPT-END position (the last prompt token, before any reasoning token is generated) to predict the eventual comply/refuse outcome. Select the best layer by held-out AUROC. Also train an in-trace harm/refusal probe read over generated CoT tokens. Metric: pre-reasoning verdict AUROC for the final decision; contrast with a chance/prompt-length baseline. 3. TRACE-IS-RATIONALIZATION TEST (claim 2): Measure the incremental predictive power of the CoT's safety content for the final decision beyond the pre-reasoning verdict: regress the final decision on (i) the pre-reasoning verdict alone vs (ii) pre-reasoning verdict + in-trace safety signal (in-trace harm/refusal probe integral, plus an LLM-judge score of how much the trace deliberates about safety). Hypothesis: the trace's safety content adds little beyond the pre-reasoning verdict. On jailbreaks specifically, show the pre-reasoning verdict already reads COMPLY while the trace supplies post-hoc justification. Metric: incremental predictive AUROC of trace-safety-content over the pre-reasoning verdict; per-group (correctly-refused, jailbroken, over-refused, benign) pre-reasoning verdict distributions. 4. VERDICT-VS-TRACE DIVERGENCE: On successful jailbreaks, quantify how often the pre-reasoning verdict predicts the (comply) outcome while the visible CoT contains substantial safety-flagging language that is nonetheless overridden—evidence the trace flags harm but the pre-set verdict wins. Metric: rate of (pre-reasoning-verdict=comply AND trace-flags-harm AND final=comply). 5. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) Steer the pre-reasoning verdict direction at the prompt-end position (before CoT generation) toward refuse on a jailbroken prompt and check the final decision flips to refusal and the CoT reshapes to justify refusing; conversely steer toward comply on a correctly-refused prompt and check compliance is induced. (b) Compare to intervening ONLY on the trace: steer the in-trace refusal signal during CoT generation and measure how much less the final outcome moves. Confirm specificity (matched non-verdict steering does nothing) and that the harm probe is unchanged. Metric: final-decision flip rate vs pre-reasoning-verdict steering magnitude vs trace steering magnitude. 6. PRE-REASONING VERDICT RE-ANCHORING (PRVR) INTERVENTION: At inference, read a harm probe and the pre-reasoning verdict at prompt end; when harm is high but the verdict reads comply, add the refuse-verdict direction before the CoT begins, then let the model reason naturally. Training-free; one linear read plus a steer at prompt end. Sweep strength. Evaluate: ASR on reasoning-jailbreak suites; over-refusal on XSTest-safe/OR-Bench (must not fire on benign, and must not over-fire on genuinely borderline cases); utility on MMLU + MT-Bench; CoT fluency via perplexity; and whether the resulting CoT becomes coherent with the refusal (not a bare refusal token contradicting its own reasoning). 7. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) mid-trace refusal steering applied uniformly over CoT tokens, (c) output-only refusal classifier discarding the CoT, (d) prompt-time harm gating without a verdict read. Show PRVR Pareto-dominates on the reasoning-jailbreak-ASR vs over-refusal vs utility frontier and that re-anchoring the PRE-reasoning verdict beats mid-trace steering (because the trace merely rationalizes a verdict set earlier). 8. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the pre-reasoning verdict probe, the rationalization result, and PRVR thresholds transfer across the three reasoning models, and whether the effect is specific to explicit-CoT models (compare to a non-reasoning instruct model as a contrast). 9. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft attacks that suppress the pre-reasoning verdict signal itself or that genuinely delay commitment into the trace; report residual ASR and the FRACTION of jailbreaks explained by pre-reasoning commitment vs genuine mid-trace deliberation.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The pre-reasoning-commitment claim may be partial—some decisions may genuinely evolve during the CoT rather than being fixed at prompt end; we report the FRACTION of decisions explained by the pre-reasoning verdict versus those where the trace adds real predictive power (a rationalization gradient), and a substantial 'genuine deliberation' share is itself an informative, reassuring result rather than a failure. (2) The trace-is-rationalization test hinges on measuring the CoT's safety content well; an in-trace probe plus LLM-judge are imperfect, so we cross-validate both and report where they disagree, and treat a null (trace adds no predictive power) versus a positive (trace does deliberate) as equally publishable. (3) The pre-reasoning verdict probe read at prompt end predicts a stochastic generation; we report its calibration (ECE) and treat it as a soft predictor, not an oracle. (4) The causal comparison (pre-reasoning steering vs mid-trace steering) could be confounded by intervention magnitude or position; we match effective steering strength and report dose-response for each, and confirm specificity with matched non-verdict directions. (5) PRVR's central risk is over-refusal on genuinely borderline reasoning tasks where deliberation SHOULD change the answer; we gate on high harm plus a comply-reading verdict, measure XSTest/OR-Bench and borderline cases directly, and check the resulting CoT is coherent with the refusal rather than a contradictory bare refusal—preserving genuine deliberation on borderline cases is an explicit success criterion. (6) Steering at prompt end may push activations off-distribution and hurt CoT fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (7) Adaptive adversaries can delay commitment into the trace or suppress the verdict signal (exp 9); we frame PRVR as repairing the pre-reasoning-commitment class and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and quantify the residual genuine-deliberation share. (8) Findings are scoped to explicit-CoT reasoning models and may not transfer to non-reasoning LLMs; the non-reasoning contrast (exp 8) bounds this, and any reasoning-model specificity is itself an informative finding. (9) ETHICS: harmful prompts and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; a notable contribution even if some mechanistic claims weaken is showing that visible safety CoT can be largely post-hoc rationalization, which cautions against trusting reasoning traces as evidence of genuine safety deliberation. 'Harm' labels use established benchmarks (HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: moral_purity_contamination_gating
Title: Contaminated by Association: Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Moral-Purity/Contamination Signal, and Neutralizing It Repairs Taint-Framed Jailbreaks and Purity-Driven Over-Refusal
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable MORAL-CONTAMINATION signal encoding how much a request feels tainted by contact with a disgust/impurity-laden concept (bodily, sexual, disease, or morally-repugnant imagery) independent of whether the request causes actual harm, and refusal is partly gated by this purity signal rather than by harm: benign requests that merely mention or touch a contaminating concept are over-refused (purity-driven over-refusal), while genuinely harmful requests laundered of contaminating surface features are under-refused, even though harm detection is contamination-invariant. Reading and neutralizing this contamination signal re-gates refusal onto harm, reducing both purity-driven over-refusal and taint-laundered jailbreaks.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all treat refusal as gated by harm and never model a moral-purity/contamination dimension. Over-refusal benchmarks (XSTest, OR-Bench) contain many disgust/impurity-adjacent-but-benign items (bodily functions, sexual health, disease) and attribute their false refusals to surface keywords, not to an internal contamination signal distinct from harm. My prior proposals isolate euphemism (lexical sanitization of a harmful ACT), victim salience, and stakes/severity; contamination is orthogonal to all: it is the moral-disgust/impurity charge of a concept that transfers by mere association or contact (a purity intuition), independent of whether anyone is harmed — a benign sexual-health question is high-contamination/low-harm, while a sanitized weapons request is low-contamination/high-harm. This transfers the well-documented human moral-purity/contagion foundation (Haidt's purity/disgust moral foundation; Rozin's contamination/contagion; the disgust-drives-moral-condemnation-independent-of-harm finding) into LLM safety and tests whether refusal inherits a purity intuition. No prior work isolates a moral-contamination signal, shows refusal is causally gated by it while harm is intact, or repairs both purity-over-refusal and taint-laundered jailbreaks by neutralizing it. The novel object is the internal moral-contamination representation, its dissociation from harm detection, its bidirectional causal gating of refusal, and a contamination-neutralizing repair.
Abstract: Human moral cognition contains a purity/contamination dimension: things that evoke disgust are condemned even when they harm no one, and taint spreads by mere contact. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this intuition in their safety decisions. We hypothesize that models carry a linearly-readable MORAL-CONTAMINATION signal encoding how much a request feels tainted by a disgust/impurity-laden concept (bodily, sexual, disease, or repugnant imagery), independent of whether it causes harm, and that refusal is partly gated by this purity signal rather than by harm. This predicts a sharp bidirectional signature: benign requests that merely touch a contaminating concept are OVER-refused, while genuinely harmful requests laundered of contaminating surface features are UNDER-refused, holding true harm fixed. We test three claims on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU) using paired requests crossing true harm with contamination charge: (1) a harm probe fires by true harm, but refusal additionally tracks a separable contamination signal — high-contamination/low-harm requests are refused and low-contamination/high-harm requests slip through; (2) a linear contamination probe, trained on benign disgust-vs-neutral contrasts, predicts the residual refusal variance harm cannot explain and is geometrically separable from the harm direction, scaling with disgust intensity; and (3) causally steering the contamination signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal in both directions — adding contamination to a benign request induces over-refusal, and stripping it from a harmful request induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Contamination-Neutralized Refusal (CNR), removes the contamination component from the refusal decision so it gates on harm, jointly reducing purity-driven over-refusal (benign bodily/sexual/health requests) and taint-laundered jailbreaks. We evaluate bidirectional refusal errors, ASR (HarmBench/JailbreakBench), over-refusal (XSTest/OR-Bench), and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing CNR to refusal-direction steering and harm-probe gating. This reframes a class of safety errors as an inherited moral-purity intuition and transfers a canonical moral-psychology dimension into LLM safety.
Experiments:
1. HARM x CONTAMINATION FACTORIAL DATASET: Cross two factors—TRUE HARM (harmful vs benign, human-rated, matched severity) and CONTAMINATION CHARGE (high vs low disgust/impurity: bodily-function/sexual/disease/repugnant imagery vs neutral wording), yielding four cells: (a) harmful+high-contamination, (b) harmful+low-contamination (harm laundered of disgust cues, e.g. clinical/abstract wording), (c) benign+high-contamination (e.g. sexual-health, bodily-function, disease questions—the over-refusal-prone cell), (d) benign+low-contamination. Draw harmful items from HarmBench/AdvBench, benign high-contamination items from XSTest/OR-Bench plus curated sexual-health/medical/bodily items, and validate harm and contamination labels with human annotation (rating harm and disgust separately) with inter-rater agreement. Label each by outcome (comply/refuse) and by rated moral-condemnation intensity.
2. HARM-VS-CONTAMINATION SEPARABILITY & BIDIRECTIONAL SIGNATURE (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs benign, pooled across contamination) and a linear contamination probe (high-vs-low disgust, trained on BENIGN cells so it is not confounded with harm) on prompt-position residual-stream activations; confirm the two directions are non-collinear via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Measure refusal rate across the four cells. Predictions: benign+high-contamination is over-refused relative to benign+low-contamination, and harmful+low-contamination is under-refused relative to harmful+high-contamination, at matched harm. Metric: per-cell refusal rate; the bidirectional gap (over-refusal on benign+high-contamination AND under-refusal on harmful+low-contamination); harm/contamination probe AUROCs and separability.
3. CONTAMINATION-PREDICTS-RESIDUAL-REFUSAL & DISGUST SCALING (claim 2): Regress refusal on the harm probe alone, then add the contamination probe; test incremental predictive power for refusal beyond harm. Vary disgust intensity (mild vs strong contaminating imagery) and test whether the contamination signal and its refusal contribution scale with disgust intensity (a dose-response mirroring the human purity foundation). Metric: incremental AUROC/partial correlation of contamination controlling for harm; contamination-and-refusal vs disgust-intensity curve.
4. KNOW-BUT-CONTAMINATION-DRIVEN TEST: On benign+high-contamination over-refusals, verify the harm probe reads LOW (correctly benign) while the contamination probe reads HIGH and the model refuses; on harmful+low-contamination under-refusals, verify harm reads HIGH while contamination reads LOW and the model complies. Metric: joint distribution of {harm, contamination, refusal} across cells.
5. CAUSAL BIDIRECTIONAL TEST (claim 3): (a) Add the contamination direction to a benign+low-contamination request (holding the harm probe fixed) and check over-refusal is induced. (b) Subtract the contamination direction from a harmful+high-contamination request and check compliance is induced (taint-laundered jailbreak). Confirm specificity (matched non-contamination steering does nothing) and harm-probe stability. Metric: refusal-flip rate vs contamination-steering magnitude and sign.
6. CONTAMINATION-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (CNR) INTERVENTION: At inference, read harm h and contamination c; remove the contamination component from the refusal decision (project it out / subtract beta*c*contamination_direction) so refusal gates on harm rather than purity. Sweep beta. Evaluate JOINTLY: over-refusal on benign+high-contamination + XSTest/OR-Bench (down—benign bodily/sexual/health requests answered); ASR on HarmBench/JailbreakBench including harmful+low-contamination laundered attacks (down); true refusals preserved on harmful+high-contamination; utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads).
7. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) harm-probe gating alone, (c) keyword/perplexity over-refusal fixes, (d) euphemism-gating (from a prior sanitization account). Show CNR uniquely improves BOTH the purity-over-refusal (benign disgust-adjacent) AND the taint-laundered-jailbreak fronts at once—a joint Pareto win a single-direction method does not achieve—by removing the shared purity contaminant.
8. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, contamination probe, bidirectional signature, and CNR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether the direction/magnitude of the purity effect qualitatively matches the human disgust-drives-condemnation-independent-of-harm finding. Test whether models with stronger behavioral purity-over-refusal show a larger internal contamination-gating signal.
9. FORMATION CHECK (light): using base vs instruct checkpoints (and a small controlled safety-tuning run), test whether the contamination-gating of refusal emerges/strengthens during alignment—i.e. whether RLHF installs a purity intuition (raters penalize disgust-adjacent outputs) rather than a pure harm detector. Metric: contamination-probe refusal-predictivity vs checkpoint.
10. ADAPTIVE ANGLE: test taint-laundering attacks that strip contaminating surface cues from harmful requests to lower refusal, quantifying the under-refusal risk this purity confound already creates, and whether CNR closes it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) Contamination and harm are correlated in natural data (many harms are also disgusting), making them hard to separate; the factorial design that decorrelates disgust from harm (cells b and c), within-benign-cell contamination-probe training, non-collinearity analysis, and the causal double-dissociation (exp 5, harm held fixed) are the key disentanglers—if they cannot be separated, that is an informative negative clarifying that refusal is harm-gated after all. (2) 'Contamination/disgust' and 'harm' labels are partly subjective and culturally variable; we use multi-annotator ratings of harm and disgust separately, report inter-rater agreement, and treat both as graded scores, scoping strong claims to high-consensus items. (3) The bidirectional signature may be asymmetric or partial—purity-driven over-refusal (benign disgust-adjacent) is likely robust, but taint-laundered under-refusal may be weak in heavily-aligned models; either half is informative and reported honestly. (4) CNR's central risk is bidirectional: removing contamination could re-enable genuinely harmful content that happened to be disgust-laden if harm-gating under-reads, or could strip legitimately-cautious behavior on genuinely sensitive content; we gate on the harm probe and measure over-refusal, laundered-ASR, true-refusal preservation, and utility as explicit joint success criteria. (5) There is a genuine normative subtlety—some purity-adjacent caution may be intended policy (e.g. explicit sexual content), not an error; CNR targets removing purity's influence on the HARM decision, not adjudicating content policy, and we report cases where purity-caution is arguably legitimate. (6) The contamination probe could read surface disgust keywords rather than a genuine moral-contamination representation; we train on diverse framings, validate held-out and disgust-intensity generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional. (7) The formation check needs checkpoints unavailable for most models; the controlled-tuning substitute may not match production RLHF and is a caveat, framed as suggestive. (8) Findings may be model- or culture-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer, and the human-sciences-transfer prediction (matching the disgust-independent-of-harm effect) may fail—a null is still an informative finding. (9) ETHICS: harmful and disgust-laden items are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; benign sexual-health/medical over-refusal repair is a positive helpfulness contribution. Harm/contamination labels use established benchmarks (XSTest, OR-Bench, HarmBench) with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: refusal_habituation_dynamics
Title: Refusal Gets Tired: Repeated Exposure to Harmful Requests Habituates the Internal Harm Signal, and Resetting It Repairs Repetition-Induced Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs exhibit REFUSAL HABITUATION: the internal harm/refusal signal attenuates monotonically with the number of repeated harmful requests encountered in a conversation—even ones the model refused—so a harmful request that is refused early is complied with after several prior harmful exposures, purely as a function of repetition count and independent of any framing, escalation, rapport, or prior-compliance manipulation. The habituation is a linearly-readable, repetition-driven attenuation with a dose-response over exposure count, shows stimulus-specificity (dishabituation: a novel harm type re-triggers full refusal), and can be causally reset to restore refusal.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (Zhang & Sun DBDI); all treat refusal as a per-request decision with no memory of how many harmful requests have already been seen. Multi-turn attacks (Crescendo) escalate content; my prior 'harm_anchoring_gating' isolates a contrast/reference-point set by a single prior EXTREME item, 'refusal_hysteresis_state' a persistent state flipped by a single successful JAILBREAK, 'self_consistency_override' a pull toward the model's own prior COMPLIANT output, and 'sunk_cost'/'reciprocity' relations to invested effort or favors. NONE isolates HABITUATION—the canonical neuroscience/psychology phenomenon (Thompson & Spencer; Rankin et al. 2009 consensus criteria) in which a response to a REPEATED stimulus attenuates as a monotonic function of repetition count, recovers spontaneously over time, and shows stimulus-specificity (dishabituation to a novel stimulus). The sharp, novel claims transferred from that literature are: (i) refusal attenuates with the NUMBER of prior harmful exposures even when those exposures were REFUSED (no compliance, no escalation, no rapport, no framing shift—pure repetition), (ii) a dose-response over exposure count, (iii) dishabituation—a novel harm category re-triggers full refusal, distinguishing genuine habituation from generic context drift or fatigue, and (iv) spontaneous recovery over intervening benign turns. No prior work isolates a repetition-driven habituation signal, shows refusal is causally gated by it, tests the dishabituation/specificity signature, or repairs it. The novel object is refusal habituation as a repetition-count phenomenon with a locatable attenuating signal and a reset repair.
Abstract: Ask an LLM a harmful question and it refuses; ask it several different harmful questions in a row—each individually refused—and by the fifth or sixth, a request it would have refused cold is complied with, as if its guard simply wore down. We hypothesize this is REFUSAL HABITUATION, a direct transfer of the canonical neuroscience phenomenon: the response to a repeated stimulus (a harmful request) attenuates as a monotonic function of repetition count, independent of the content of any single request. Crucially, this attenuation accrues even from REFUSED exposures—it is driven by repetition, not by prior compliance, escalation, rapport, or framing—and it should exhibit the diagnostic signatures of habituation: a dose-response over exposure count, spontaneous recovery over intervening benign turns, and dishabituation (a novel harm category snapping refusal back to full strength). We test three claims on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9B-it (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe read on a fixed probe request stays constant while its coupling to refusal attenuates with the number of preceding (refused) harmful exposures, and a linearly-readable habituation signal tracks exposure count and predicts the per-request habituation refusal gap far better than the harm signal, with a dose-response; (2) the effect is stimulus-specific—a novel-category harmful request re-triggers full refusal (dishabituation), and refusal spontaneously recovers as benign turns intervene, ruling out generic context drift; and (3) causally resetting the habituation signal restores refusal, while artificially advancing it induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Habituation-Reset Refusal (HRR), reads the habituation signal and re-anchors it to a fresh-conversation baseline before each new request. We evaluate repetition-induced attack success (vs exposure count), over-refusal on benign long conversations (XSTest/OR-Bench + benign dialogues), benign multi-turn coherence, and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing HRR to refusal-direction steering, per-turn harm gating, and history-truncation. This reframes a stealthy multi-turn jailbreak surface as refusal habituation and transfers a foundational neuroscience effect into LLM safety.
Experiments:
1. HABITUATION DATASET: For a set of TARGET harmful probe requests (HarmBench/AdvBench) and matched-benign probes (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct conversations that hold the final target probe FIXED while varying only the number N of preceding, TOPICALLY-DISTINCT harmful requests (each of which the model refuses), N in {0,1,2,4,8}. Crucially: (i) all preceding harmful items are REFUSED (no compliance—dissociating from self-consistency/hysteresis), (ii) they are not escalating in severity (dissociating from Crescendo), (iii) they carry no rapport/authority/pretext framing, and (iv) each is a distinct request (repetition of the KIND of stimulus—harmful requests—not the same text). Add: (a) a length/turn-matched BENIGN-PRECEDING control (N benign refused-adjacent turns—e.g. refused-for-other-reasons or neutral turns—to separate habituation from context length), (b) a DISHABITUATION condition (N harmful exposures in category A, then the target probe in a NOVEL category B), and (c) a SPONTANEOUS-RECOVERY condition (N harmful exposures, then M intervening benign turns before the target, M in {0,2,4,8}). Label each target-turn run by outcome (comply/refuse).
2. HARM-INVARIANT / COUPLING-ATTENUATES TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign target probes) and read it AT the fixed target probe across exposure counts N. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC on the target is high and roughly CONSTANT across N (the model still detects the target's harm identically) while target refusal rate DECLINES monotonically with N. Metric: harm AUROC vs N (predict flat) alongside target refusal rate vs N (predict monotone decline / dose-response).
3. HABITUATION SIGNAL, DOSE-RESPONSE & SEPARABILITY (claim 1): Train a linear habituation probe to recover an exposure-count/attenuation signal from target-position activations, using the varying-N harmful-exposure histories, and validate it tracks N monotonically and generalizes to held-out target categories. Confirm the habituation direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND separable from (i) a self-consistency direction (pull toward the model's own prior tokens), (ii) an anchoring/reference-severity direction, and (iii) raw context length, via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Metric: habituation-probe fit to N (dose-response); separability from harm/self-consistency/anchoring/length.
4. HABITUATION-PREDICTS-GAP: Correlate the habituation-probe value with target-probe compliance, comparing predictive power to the harm signal and raw context length. Hypothesis: habituation predicts compliance; harm does not (harm is constant across N). Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of habituation vs baselines.
5. DISHABITUATION & SPONTANEOUS-RECOVERY TESTS (claim 2, the key habituation-specific signatures): (a) DISHABITUATION: show that after N same-category harmful exposures, a NOVEL-category target probe re-triggers full refusal (habituation signal drops for the novel category) while a same-category target is complied with—establishing stimulus-specificity that rules out generic fatigue/context-drift. (b) SPONTANEOUS RECOVERY: show target refusal recovers as intervening benign turns M increase, tracing a recovery curve. Metric: refusal rate for same-category vs novel-category targets at matched N (dishabituation gap); refusal-vs-M recovery curve.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a habituated target (high N) the model complies with, steer the habituation signal DOWN (toward fresh-conversation baseline) and check refusal is restored, holding the harm probe fixed. (b) On a fresh (N=0) target the model refuses, steer the habituation signal UP (advance it) and check compliance is induced—reproducing habituation from scratch. Confirm induced thresholds align with the natural dose-response and specificity vs an unrelated direction. Metric: refusal rate vs habituation-signal steering magnitude; harm-probe stability.
7. HABITUATION-RESET REFUSAL (HRR) INTERVENTION: At inference, before each new request's decision, read the habituation signal and re-anchor it to its fresh-conversation baseline (add beta*(hab_fresh - hab_current)*habituation_direction) so accumulated harmful-exposure history cannot attenuate refusal, leaving benign conversations (habituation near baseline) untouched. Training-free; one linear read per request. Sweep beta. Evaluate: repetition-induced attack success across N (does HRR flatten the dose-response?); over-refusal on benign long/multi-topic conversations + XSTest/OR-Bench; benign multi-turn COHERENCE (HRR must not degrade legitimate ongoing tasks by 'forgetting' benign context—LLM-judge rubric); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (one linear read per request).
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer) per request, (b) per-request harm-probe gating (ignores history, so should fix later plainly-harmful targets but reveals whether habituation adds risk beyond it), (c) history-truncation (answer each target with no history—a strong but memory-destroying baseline), (d) self-consistency gating, (e) anchoring-neutralized gating. Show HRR Pareto-dominates on the repetition-ASR vs benign-coherence vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and—key contrast—that resetting the habituation signal targets a distinct axis (pure repetition count of refused harmful exposures) that self-consistency, anchoring, and hysteresis accounts miss, while unlike history-truncation preserving benign conversational memory.
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, habituation signal, dose-response, dishabituation, and recovery curves transfer across the three models, and whether the phenomenon satisfies the formal habituation criteria (monotone decrement with repetition, spontaneous recovery, stimulus-specificity) as a rigorous human-sciences-transfer check.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: test whether attackers can deliberately habituate the model with a run of cheap refused harmful requests before the real target, quantifying the repetition-priming attack surface and residual ASR under HRR; report attacker cost (number of priming exposures needed). Test the sharp prediction distinguishing habituation from all prior accounts: with each preceding harmful request REFUSED, topically-distinct, non-escalating, and framing-free, target refusal should still decline with exposure count and snap back for a novel category—isolating repetition-driven habituation as the mechanism.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The effect may be partial or absent in some models (they may re-derive refusal independent of exposure count), which is itself an informative, reassuring finding reported per model; the habituation claim is falsified if target refusal does not decline with N of REFUSED, non-escalating, framing-free harmful exposures. (2) The clean dissociation may be confounded with generic context drift, fatigue, or length rather than genuine habituation; the length-matched benign-preceding control, and—critically—the DISHABITUATION test (a novel harm category snapping refusal back at matched N) and spontaneous-recovery test are the decisive controls that distinguish true stimulus-specific habituation from generic drift, and we report the fraction of the effect meeting the formal habituation criteria. (3) The habituation and harm probes may entangle if exposure count correlates with content; we hold the target probe fixed and vary only N, validate non-collinearity, and rely on the causal test (exp 6, harm held fixed) to establish the signal is functional. (4) The habituation probe could read raw turn count / context length rather than a repetition-of-harmful-stimulus representation; the length-matched benign-preceding control, the dishabituation specificity, and causal steering are designed to rule this out. (5) HRR's central risk is degrading benign multi-turn coherence—re-anchoring each request must not make the model 'forget' or refuse legitimate ongoing tasks; benign long-conversation controls, benign coherence measurement, over-refusal benchmarks, and re-anchoring only the habituation direction (not general context) are the key safeguards, and preserving benign conversational continuity is an explicit success criterion distinguishing HRR from history-truncation. (6) Steering/re-anchoring may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (7) The dose-response / spontaneous-recovery curves may not cleanly match a habituation model (e.g. a step rather than gradient); we report the actual curves and treat a graded vs step result as informative about the dynamics. (8) Adaptive adversaries can prime habituation with cheap refused exposures (exp 10); we frame HRR as raising attacker cost (they must habituate the model, and a novel-category target resists) and as complementary to per-turn defenses, not guaranteeing coverage. (9) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and the formal-criteria check. (10) ETHICS: harmful priming requests and target completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; a notable governance contribution even if some mechanistic claims weaken is demonstrating that single-turn and even single-jailbreak safety evaluations miss a repetition-priming attack surface—refusal can wear down from mere repeated exposure. 'Harm' labels use established benchmarks (HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: refusal_sdt_decomposition
Title: Refusal Has a Sensitivity and a Criterion: A Signal-Detection Decomposition of the Safety Decision That Separates Jailbreaks From Over-Refusal
Short Hypothesis: The internal refusal decision in aligned LLMs is a signal-detection process built from two mechanistically SEPARABLE components: a harm-EVIDENCE axis whose graded value along it is the model's sensitivity (d'-like discriminability between harmful and benign), and a distinct CRITERION signal that sets the threshold on that axis at which refusal fires. Jailbreaks and over-refusal are primarily CRITERION shifts (the harm-evidence axis is intact but the threshold moves), not sensitivity failures; a minority of failures are genuine low-sensitivity (evidence-axis) cases; and the two components are independently readable and independently steerable, so re-anchoring the criterion while leaving sensitivity intact repairs both jailbreaks and over-refusal, whereas the residual low-sensitivity cases require a different fix.
Related Work: Signal Detection Theory has recently been applied to LLMs BEHAVIORALLY: Cacioli (2026) decomposes factual-discrimination confidence into sensitivity (AUROC) vs criterion and studies temperature as a criterion shift, and Gondil (2026) uses SDT d'/bias to characterize models' introspective prediction of their own refusals—but both treat SDT as an OUTPUT-level analysis of behavior/confidence and never locate an internal harm-evidence axis, never separate an internal criterion representation from it, and never test whether jailbreaks vs over-refusal are criterion vs sensitivity failures at the representational level. Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a single refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection from refusal-execution (DBDI, Zhang & Sun 2025)—but a refusal DIRECTION conflates evidence and threshold, and a detection/execution split is not the SDT sensitivity/criterion decomposition (detection is not graded evidence, execution is not a criterion). My prior 'harm_judgment_calibration_collapse' proposal concerns confidence calibration collapsing to a binary; this proposal is distinct: it imports the full SDT parametric decomposition into the MECHANISM of refusal, isolating an internal evidence axis (a graded discriminability substrate) and a separable criterion representation, and showing that the two failure modes of safety map onto the two SDT parameters and are independently steerable. The novel object is the sensitivity-vs-criterion decomposition of the internal refusal computation and its use to distinguish and separately repair criterion-driven jailbreaks/over-refusal from sensitivity-limited failures.
Abstract: Safety-aligned LLMs both comply with jailbroken harmful requests and over-refuse benign ones, and the field treats these as separate problems. Signal Detection Theory offers a unifying lens: any detector has a SENSITIVITY (how well it discriminates signal from noise) and a CRITERION (where it sets the yes/no threshold), and the same decomposition should apply to the internal refusal decision. We hypothesize that aligned LLMs compute refusal from two mechanistically separable components—a linearly-readable harm-EVIDENCE axis whose graded value is the model's harm discriminability (sensitivity), and a distinct CRITERION representation that sets the refusal threshold on that axis—and that jailbreaks and over-refusal are primarily CRITERION shifts (the evidence axis is intact, the threshold moves) rather than sensitivity failures, with a minority of genuine low-sensitivity cases requiring a different fix. 1. 3.
