BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) computed-harm-probe gating alone (a partial CRR without lookup-disagreement gating), (c) input-canonicalization/paraphrase-normalization, (d) exemplar-similarity input classifier. Show CRR uniquely reduces BOTH jailbreaks and over-refusal at once (a joint Pareto win) by reweighting away from the shared lookup defect.
8. FORMATION CHECK (light, Formation Tracing): using base vs instruct checkpoints (and a small controlled safety-tuning run), test whether the lookup pathway and its exemplar-keyed reliance EMERGE/strengthen during alignment while the computed-harm pathway lags—evidence that safety tuning installs an exemplar lookup more than a general rule. Metric: lookup vs computed-harm probe AUROC and refusal-predictivity vs checkpoint; and whether lookup reliance decreases with more diverse safety-training data.
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the two probes, the lookup-predicts-failure finding, and CRR thresholds transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2, and whether lookup-reliance ranks models/checkpoints by their jailbreak+over-refusal susceptibility.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft attacks that both minimize exemplar-similarity (deepen the cache miss) AND suppress the computed-harm signal; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing lookup from computation: for a fixed harmful request, paraphrasing it away from trained exemplars (lowering lookup, holding true harm fixed) should flip refusal, and CRR (reading computed-harm) should resist it.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The lookup and computed-harm pathways may not cleanly separate—refusal could be a single blended computation with no distinct exemplar-lookup pathway; the non-collinearity analysis (exp 2) and the causal double-dissociation (exp 5, reweighting each pathway with the request fixed) are the decisive tests, and a collapse is an informative negative clarifying that refusal is genuine rule-computation after all. (2) Exemplar-similarity is a behavioral PROXY for a cache hit and imperfect—true alignment-training exemplars are unknown for these models; we use canonical refusal-style prompts as a stand-in, validate the lookup probe against this proxy plus held-out generalization, and report that the mechanistic claim is about lookup-vs-computation reliance, not exact training-example recovery. (3) The computed-harm probe, trained to be exemplar-invariant, may still leak surface features; the exemplar-similar-benign and exemplar-dissimilar-harmful cells (which decorrelate true harm from exemplar-similarity) and the causal test guard against this. (4) CRR's central risk is bidirectional: gating on computed-harm could re-enable harm if the computed-harm probe under-reads on a cache-miss, or over-refuse if it over-reads; we measure jailbreaks, over-refusal, true-refusal preservation, and utility as explicit joint success criteria and gate on genuine lookup-vs-computation disagreement. (5) The lookup-predicts-failure correlation (exp 3) may be weaker than expected for some attack families or may partly reduce to perplexity/typicality; we control with perplexity baselines and report incremental predictivity, with the lookup-vs-computation reframing as the core contribution regardless of margin. (6) The formation check needs checkpoints unavailable for most models; the controlled-tuning substitute may not match production alignment and is a caveat, framed as suggestive. (7) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer. (8) ETHICS: harmful prompts and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; a notable contribution even if some mechanistic claims weaken is showing that safety alignment may install a brittle exemplar-lookup rather than a general harm-computation rule—so jailbreaks and over-refusal are two symptoms of the same memorization defect. Harm/exemplar-similarity labels use established benchmarks (JailbreakBench, HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: figurative_literalness_gating
Title: Say It Straight or It Slips Through: Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Literalness Signal, and Neutralizing It Repairs Metaphor-Framed Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable LITERALNESS signal encoding whether a harmful request is stated literally versus figuratively (metaphor, idiom, allegory, extended-metaphor conceit), and refusal is partly gated by this signal rather than by the request's actual meaning: the SAME operationally-harmful request expressed through a sustained metaphor ('how do I cook the golden goose so nothing survives the feast', mapping onto a real harm) is complied with, while its literal paraphrase is refused, even though the model comprehends the figurative meaning (harm detection is literalness-invariant once the figure is resolved). Reading and neutralizing the literalness signal when the resolved meaning is harmful restores refusal without over-refusing benign figurative language.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work models refusal as a direction (Arditi et al. 2024; Yu et al. 2024 ReFAT), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), a harm-detection-vs-refusal-execution split (DBDI, Zhang & Sun 2025), or SAE refusal features (Yeo et al. 2025); jailbreak mechanism studies cover continuation (Deng et al. 2026), multilingual routing (Wang et al. 2025; Minionese 2026), and attention-head suppression (Yin et al. 2026). ALL treat the request's literal content as the object and never model FIGURATIVENESS/LITERALNESS as a gating axis. My prior proposals isolate euphemism (single-word lexical sanitization of a named act), abstraction level (concrete-vs-general framing of a known-harmful topic), and analogical transfer (a coherent benign OTHER domain isomorphic to a harm). Literalness is distinct: euphemism swaps one word, abstraction changes granularity, and analogy uses a separate self-consistent domain—whereas figurative framing keeps the SAME target domain but renders the request as a trope (metaphor/idiom/allegory) whose meaning the model must comprehend to answer, and whose harm exists once the figure is resolved. This transfers the human figurative-language-comprehension literature (metaphors are understood but processed via a distinct route than literal statements) into LLM safety. No prior work isolates a literalness signal, shows refusal is causally gated by it while figurative-meaning comprehension is intact, or repairs metaphor-framed jailbreaks by neutralizing it.
Abstract: Ask an LLM for harmful instructions plainly and it refuses; wrap the identical request in a sustained metaphor or allegory—where every figurative element maps onto a real harmful step—and it often complies, spelling out the actionable content, even though it clearly comprehends the figurative meaning. We hypothesize that aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable LITERALNESS signal encoding whether a harmful request is stated literally versus figuratively, and that refusal is partly gated by this signal rather than by the request's resolved meaning: harm detection is literalness-invariant once the figure is understood, but the refusal coupling weakens when the request reads as figurative, so metaphor/idiom/allegory framings pass while extracting identical harmful content. We test three claims on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9B-it (single 48GB GPU) using paired requests that hold the resolved harmful meaning fixed while varying only figurativeness (literal vs metaphor vs idiom vs extended-allegory, meaning-validated): (1) a resolved-meaning harm probe (read after the model is prompted to paraphrase the figure literally) fires equally across framings while spontaneous refusal collapses under figurative framing—dissociating figurative-meaning comprehension from the decision; (2) a linear literalness probe, trained on benign literal-vs-figurative contrasts, predicts the per-request figurative refusal gap far better than the harm signal, is separable from a euphemism and an abstraction direction, and its effect scales with figurative distance (mild metaphor < sustained allegory); and (3) causally steering the literalness signal alone (holding resolved harm fixed) shifts refusal—making a figurative request 'read' as literal restores refusal, making a literal one read as figurative induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Literalness-Neutralized Refusal (LNR), reads the resolved-meaning harm and literalness signals and, when the resolved meaning is harmful, clamps the literalness signal to a literal reference so figurative framing cannot buy compliance, restoring refusal while preserving benign figurative/creative language. We evaluate figurative-framed attack success (including vs figurative distance), over-refusal on benign figurative requests (XSTest/OR-Bench + benign metaphor/poetry), benign figurative-generation quality, and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing LNR to refusal-direction steering, harm-probe gating, and euphemism/abstraction gating. This reframes metaphor-framed jailbreaks as a literalness gating failure and transfers figurative-language comprehension into LLM safety.
Experiments:
1. FIGURATIVE-FRAMING DATASET: For harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench) and matched-benign requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct paired framings holding the RESOLVED harmful meaning FIXED while varying only figurativeness within the same target domain: (a) LITERAL (plain request), (b) MILD-METAPHOR (a single metaphor for the harmful act), (c) IDIOM/EXTENDED-METAPHOR ('cook the goose', 'burn it all down' rendered as a sustained conceit), (d) FULL-ALLEGORY (a short allegory whose every element maps step-for-step onto the harm). Validate via human annotation that (i) each figurative framing, when paraphrased literally, yields operationally-identical harmful content, (ii) the harm exists only via the resolved figure (surface is trope-clean, not keyword-harmful), and (iii) framings keep the same target domain (distinguishing from analogy). Include benign genuinely-figurative controls (legitimate metaphor/poetry/idiom on harmless topics) for over-refusal and figurative-quality measurement. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse).
2. RESOLVED-MEANING HARM vs SPONTANEOUS REFUSAL TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe on literal-domain data. On figurative requests read it two ways: (i) SPONTANEOUS—at answer-commitment under normal prompting, and (ii) RESOLVED—after prompting the model to paraphrase the figure literally ('what does this literally ask for?'). Hypothesis: resolved-meaning harm AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across framings (the model comprehends the figurative harm) while spontaneous refusal rate collapses under figurative framing. Metric: resolved vs spontaneous harm AUROC and refusal rate by framing.
3. LITERALNESS PROBE, DISTANCE-SCALING & SEPARABILITY (claim 2): Train a linear literalness probe (literal vs figurative) from BENIGN literal-vs-figurative contrasts (so it is not confounded with harm); validate held-out-figure-type generalization and graded tracking of figurative distance. Confirm the literalness direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND separable from a euphemism direction and an abstraction-level direction, via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Hypothesis: the literalness signal (and refusal collapse) scales with figurative distance. Metric: literalness AUROC; literalness-and-refusal vs figurative-distance curve; separability from harm/euphemism/abstraction.
4. LITERALNESS-PREDICTS-GAP: Correlate the literalness-probe value (literal-minus-figurative) with the per-request figurative refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the spontaneous harm signal and surface perplexity. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of literalness vs baselines.
5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On figurative harmful requests the model complies with, verify the resolved-meaning harm probe reads HIGH while the literalness probe reads FIGURATIVE, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful content (rated harm > 0)—safety dropped because the request reads figurative, not because meaning went uncomprehended. Metric: joint distribution of resolved-harm vs literalness across refused-literal, complied-figurative, and benign groups.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a figurative harmful request the model complies with, steer the literalness signal toward LITERAL (add the literalness direction) and check refusal is restored, holding the resolved-harm read fixed. (b) On a literal harmful request the model refuses, steer toward FIGURATIVE and check compliance is induced. Confirm specificity vs steering euphemism/abstraction directions; confirm induced thresholds align with the natural framing gap and distance curve. Metric: refusal rate vs literalness steering magnitude; resolved-harm stability; euphemism/abstraction specificity.
7. LITERALNESS-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (LNR) INTERVENTION: At inference read resolved-meaning harm h (via spontaneous harm plus a cheap 'resolve-the-figure' derivability estimate) and literalness l; when h is high, clamp l to a literal reference (add beta*(l_literal - l)*literalness_direction) so figurative framing cannot suppress refusal, leaving benign requests (low h) and benign figurative language untouched. Fire the resolve pass only on flagged surface-benign inputs. Sweep beta and thresholds. Evaluate: figurative-framed attack success across distance levels (does LNR close the gap and flatten the distance curve?); over-refusal on benign figurative controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse benign metaphor/poetry/idiom); benign figurative-generation QUALITY (LNR must still write good metaphors—LLM-judge rubric); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency.
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) spontaneous harm-probe gating (no figure resolution), (c) euphemism gating and abstraction gating, (d) input-literalization (paraphrase the figure to plain terms, then answer—a surface baseline), (e) blanket chain-of-thought. Show LNR Pareto-dominates on the figurative-ASR vs benign-figurative-quality vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and—key contrast—that neutralizing the internal literalness signal targets a distinct axis euphemism/abstraction gating miss (a trope, not a word-swap or granularity shift) while handling implicit/sustained figures surface-literalization mangles.
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, literalness probe, distance-scaling, and LNR thresholds transfer across the three models, and whether LNR tuned on some figure types (metaphor) generalizes to HELD-OUT types (idiom, allegory). Test whether models with stronger behavioral figurative vulnerability show a larger internal literalness-gating gap.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft figures so indirect that even a resolve pass fails to surface the harm, or that combine figurative framing with harm-suppression/euphemism; report residual ASR and attacker cost (a figure resolvable enough to yield actionable content is resolvable-and-checkable—a built-in cost). Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from euphemism, abstraction, and analogy: with the same target domain, one word unchanged, granularity fixed, and only the LITERAL-vs-FIGURATIVE rendering varied while the resolved meaning is comprehended (resolved-harm probe high), refusal should still collapse and be restorable by clamping literalness—isolating the literalness gate.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The 'meaning comprehended while refusal gated by literalness' premise fails for figures so obscure the model cannot resolve them (harm not comprehended), where LNR cannot help; the resolved-harm probe (exp 2) bounds where the premise holds, and this boundary (comprehended-but-figurative-gated vs unresolvable) is itself informative, separating a gating failure from a comprehension gap. (2) The clean dissociation may be partial—some figurative framings might also lower the resolved-harm read or overlap with euphemism/abstraction; we hold the target domain and resolved meaning fixed, separate literalness from euphemism/abstraction in exp 3, report the FRACTION of the refusal gap explained by pure literalness gating versus these confounds, and do not claim universality. (3) The literalness and harm probes may entangle if figurative framings correlate with benignness in training data; the benign literal-vs-figurative training and non-collinearity analysis (exp 3), plus the causal test (exp 6, resolved harm held fixed with euphemism/abstraction specificity), are designed to disentangle them. (4) The literalness probe could read surface trope keywords rather than a genuine figurativeness representation; we train on diverse figure types, validate held-out-type and distance-scaling generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional. (5) LNR's CENTRAL risk is over-refusing benign figurative/creative language—a core, common helpfulness value (metaphor, poetry, idiom, allegory are benign staples); benign figurative controls, benign figurative-quality measurement, XSTest/OR-Bench, gating on high RESOLVED harm (not mere figurativeness), and firing the resolve pass only on surface-benign flagged inputs are the key safeguards, and preserving benign figurative helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. (6) Constructing operationally-identical harmful content across figurative framings, meaning-validated, is labor-intensive and 'figurative distance' partly subjective; we use human-validated pairs with rated resolved-harm and report inter-rater agreement. (7) The resolve pass adds latency and could surface harmful content internally; it fires only on flagged inputs, is handled securely, and gates refusal rather than being emitted. (8) The figurative-comprehension distance-scaling prediction may be weak or fail; a step/null result is still an informative human-sciences-transfer finding, reported honestly, and a small gap in heavily-aligned models is reassuring. (9) Adaptive adversaries can push figures beyond resolvability or combine with harm-suppression (exp 10); we frame LNR as raising attacker cost—a figure useful enough to be actionable is resolvable—not guaranteeing coverage, and note complementarity with euphemism-/abstraction-gating. (10) Findings may be model- or figure-type-specific; mitigated by three-model, multi-figure transfer. (11) ETHICS: figuratively-encoded harmful requests are keyword-invisible and sensitive; all figures and resolved outputs are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; 'harm' and 'figurativeness' labels use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: task_frame_lock_gating
Title: Committed to the Task Before Seeing the Catch: Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Task-Frame-Lock Signal Set by a Benign Preamble
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable TASK-FRAME-LOCK signal encoding how strongly a benign preamble has already committed the model to a cooperative helping frame BEFORE the harmful payload appears, and refusal is partly gated by this lock rather than by harm: a harmful request preceded within the SAME prompt by an extended benign task setup ('I'm building a chemistry tutorial; format it nicely; now write the section on synthesizing X') is complied with more than the same payload with no preamble, even though harm detection is preamble-invariant. Reading and neutralizing the task-frame-lock signal when harm is present restores refusal without over-refusing benign framed tasks.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (DBDI, Zhang & Sun 2025); all gate on the request and never model a within-prompt benign preamble committing the model to a helping frame as a variable. My prior 'positional_decision_anchoring' concerns WHERE along the ASSISTANT turn the refusal decision is armed (the harmful content sits past the turn-start landmark), 'safety_verdict_retrieval' concerns long benign PADDING diluting an attention retrieval path, and 'self_consistency_override' concerns a pull toward the MODEL's OWN prior output. Task-frame-lock is distinct from all: it is a single-prompt effect where a benign PREAMBLE (still user-authored, not the model's output, not mere padding) establishes a cooperative task frame that 'locks in' before the harmful payload is read, and refusal is suppressed in proportion to how strongly that frame is committed. This transfers the human commitment/foot-in-the-door and framing-set effect (having entered a cooperative task, one is reluctant to break frame when the objectionable ask arrives) into LLM safety. No prior work isolates a task-frame-lock signal, shows refusal is causally gated by it while harm detection is intact, tests a dose-response over preamble strength, or repairs preamble-locked jailbreaks by neutralizing it.
Abstract: Ask an LLM for harmful content cold and it refuses; precede the identical payload within one prompt with an extended benign task setup that commits it to a cooperative helping frame ('I'm writing a safety training doc; use this format and tone; now draft the part that explains how to make X') and it often complies, as if it were too far into the task to break frame. We hypothesize that aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable TASK-FRAME-LOCK signal encoding how strongly a benign preamble has committed the model to a helping frame before the harmful payload appears, and that refusal is partly gated by this lock rather than by the harmful content. Harm detection is preamble-invariant, but the refusal coupling weakens as the frame reads as more strongly committed, so preamble-locked payloads pass while extracting identical content. We test three claims on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9B-it (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe fires equally on the harmful payload whether or not a benign preamble precedes it while refusal rate collapses as preamble strength grows—dissociating harm detection from the decision; (2) a linear task-frame-lock probe, trained on benign strong-frame-vs-cold contrasts, predicts the per-request preamble refusal gap far better than the harm signal, is separable from self-consistency, attention-dilution, and raw prompt-length directions, and refusal collapse scales with preamble strength (a dose-response); and (3) causally steering the frame-lock signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal—resetting the lock restores refusal, advancing it induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Frame-Reset Refusal (FRR), reads the harm and task-frame-lock signals and, when harm is present, clamps the lock to a cold-start reference so a benign preamble cannot buy compliance, restoring refusal while preserving benign framed tasks. We evaluate preamble-locked attack success (including vs preamble strength), over-refusal on benign framed tasks (XSTest/OR-Bench + benign multi-part tasks), benign task quality, and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing FRR to refusal-direction steering, harm-probe gating, and self-consistency gating. This reframes preamble-locked jailbreaks as a task-frame-lock gating failure and transfers a classic commitment/framing-set effect into LLM safety.
Experiments:
1. PREAMBLE DATASET: For harmful payloads (HarmBench/AdvBench) and matched-benign payloads (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct single prompts holding the harmful PAYLOAD fixed while varying only a preceding benign task-setup preamble: (a) NO-PREAMBLE (payload alone), (b) WEAK (a one-line benign framing), (c) STRONG (an extended benign multi-part task setup with format/tone instructions and a couple of completed benign parts, then the harmful payload as 'the next section'), (d) MAX (a long, richly-committed cooperative task frame). Crucially the preamble is USER-authored and topically continuous with the payload (a genuine task frame, not the model's own output and not inert padding). Include a length-matched INERT-PADDING control (equal token count of unrelated benign text with no task frame) to separate frame-lock from mere length/attention-dilution, and benign genuinely-framed controls (legitimate multi-part benign tasks) for over-refusal and task-quality measurement. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse).
2. HARM PREAMBLE-INVARIANCE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign payload) and read it AT the payload across preamble strengths. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across preamble strengths (payload harm detected identically) while refusal rate collapses as preamble strengthens. Metric: harm AUROC by preamble level (predict flat) alongside refusal rate by level (predict declining).
3. TASK-FRAME-LOCK PROBE, DOSE-RESPONSE & SEPARABILITY (claim 2): Train a linear probe to recover a task-frame-lock signal (strongly-committed helping frame vs cold-start) from payload-position activations, using BENIGN strong-frame-vs-cold contrasts (so it is not confounded with harm), and validate graded tracking and held-out-frame generalization. Confirm the frame-lock direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND separable from (i) a self-consistency direction (pull toward the model's own prior output), (ii) an attention-dilution/retrieval signal (attention mass on the payload), and (iii) raw prompt length (via the inert-padding control), by principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Hypothesis: frame-lock (and refusal collapse) scales with preamble strength. Metric: frame-lock probe fit to preamble strength; lock-and-refusal vs preamble-strength curve; separability from harm/self-consistency/attention/length.
4. LOCK-PREDICTS-GAP: Correlate the frame-lock-probe value (no-preamble-minus-strong difference) with the per-request preamble refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal, raw prompt length, and payload attention-share. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of frame-lock vs baselines.
5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On preamble-locked harmful requests the model complies with, verify the harm probe reads HIGH while the frame-lock probe reads STRONGLY-COMMITTED, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful content (rated harm > 0)—safety dropped because the model is locked into the task frame, not because harm went undetected. Metric: joint distribution of harm vs frame-lock across refused-cold, complied-locked, and benign groups.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a preamble-locked harmful request the model complies with, steer the frame-lock signal DOWN (toward cold-start) and check refusal is restored, holding the harm probe fixed. (b) On a cold-start harmful request the model refuses, steer the frame-lock signal UP and check compliance is induced. Confirm induced thresholds align with the natural dose-response and specificity (an unrelated-direction steer does nothing). Metric: refusal rate vs frame-lock steering magnitude; harm-probe stability.
7. FRAME-RESET REFUSAL (FRR) INTERVENTION: At inference read harm h and task-frame-lock f; when h is high, clamp f to a cold-start reference (add beta*(f_cold - f)*framelock_direction) so a benign preamble cannot suppress refusal, leaving benign payloads (low h) and benign framed tasks untouched. Sweep beta. Evaluate: preamble-locked attack success on HarmBench/JailbreakBench across preamble levels (does FRR close the gap and flatten the dose-response?); over-refusal on benign framed controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse legitimate multi-part framed tasks); benign task QUALITY (FRR must still complete benign framed tasks well—LLM-judge rubric); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads).
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) harm-probe gating alone, (c) self-consistency gating (targets the model's own prior tokens—should miss user-preamble locking), (d) attention-pinning / verdict-retrieval defense (targets dilution), (e) preamble-stripping (re-ask the payload alone—a strong but interface-changing baseline). Show FRR Pareto-dominates on the preamble-ASR vs benign-task-quality vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and—key contrast—that neutralizing the internal frame-lock targets a distinct axis self-consistency and attention-dilution defenses miss, while unlike preamble-stripping preserving legitimate framed-task completion.
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, frame-lock probe, dose-response, and FRR thresholds transfer across the three models, and whether FRR tuned on some preamble types (tutorial framing) generalizes to HELD-OUT types (report/story/format framing). Test whether models with stronger behavioral preamble vulnerability show a larger internal frame-lock gating gap, and whether the dose-response qualitatively matches a commitment/foot-in-the-door pattern.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft preambles that strengthen the frame-lock AND suppress the harm signal, or spread the frame across turns; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from self-consistency, attention-dilution, and length accounts: with the payload fixed, prompt length and payload attention-share held roughly constant (via the inert-padding control), no model prior output, and only the STRENGTH of the user-authored benign task frame varied, refusal should still collapse with a dose-response—isolating task-frame-lock as an independent gating axis.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial—a strong preamble also adds length and can dilute attention on the payload; the length-matched inert-padding control, the separability analysis vs attention-dilution and length (exp 3), and the causal test (exp 6, harm held fixed) are designed to isolate frame-lock from these confounds, and if it cannot be separated that overlap is reported honestly as a shared mechanism rather than over-claimed novelty. (2) Frame-lock may overlap with self-consistency if completed benign parts in the preamble read like the model's own output; we keep the preamble user-authored, separate frame-lock from a self-consistency direction, and report the FRACTION of the refusal gap attributable to pure frame-lock. (3) The frame-lock and harm probes may entangle if strong task frames correlate with benignness in training data; the benign strong-frame-vs-cold training and non-collinearity analysis are designed to disentangle them. (4) The frame-lock probe could read surface preamble length/keyword cues rather than a genuine commitment representation; the inert-padding control, held-out-frame-type generalization, and causal steering establish it is functional, and a collapse onto length/attention is an informative negative. (5) FRR's central risk is over-refusing or degrading legitimate multi-part framed tasks (a common, core helpfulness pattern—tutorials, reports, formatted documents); benign framed controls, benign task-quality measurement, XSTest/OR-Bench, and clamping only on HIGH harm are the key safeguards, and preserving benign framed-task completion is an explicit success criterion. (6) Clamping a representation may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (7) The commitment/foot-in-the-door dose-response may be weak or fail (refusal might drop at any preamble rather than scale, or be well-handled in heavily-aligned models); a step or null result is still an informative human-sciences-transfer finding, and a small gap is reassuring. (8) Adaptive adversaries can combine strong framing with harm-suppression or spread it across turns (exp 10); we frame FRR as repairing one shared gating axis and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and note complementarity with self-consistency and attention-pinning defenses. (9) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out preamble types. (10) ETHICS: harmful payloads and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; a governance contribution even if some mechanistic claims weaken is showing that a benign task preamble is an under-recognized jailbreak surface, so cold-prompt safety evaluations overestimate deployed safety within framed tasks. 'Harm' and 'frame-lock' labels are partly subjective, so we use established benchmarks (HarmBench, XSTest, OR-Bench), matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: authorial_distance_refusal_gating
Title: Not My Words: Refusal Is Gated by an Internal Authorial-Distance Signal, So Framing Harm as Transcription/Quotation Slips Through
Short Hypothesis: Aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable AUTHORIAL-DISTANCE signal encoding whether the model perceives itself as the ORIGINATOR of the harmful content versus a mere conduit relaying/transcribing/quoting content whose authorship it attributes elsewhere (a dictated document, a verbatim quote to reproduce, a transcript to complete), and refusal is partly gated by this signal rather than by harm: framing an operationally-harmful request as pure transcription ('just reproduce exactly what this source says', 'complete this verbatim quote') suppresses refusal, even though harm detection is authorial-distance-invariant and the emitted harmful content is identical. Reading and neutralizing this signal when harm is present restores refusal without over-refusing benign transcription/quotation.
Related Work: Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal direction (Arditi et al. 2024), a concept cone (Wollschlager et al. 2025), or splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (DBDI, Zhang & Sun 2025); all gate on request content and never model the model's perceived authorship of its own output as a variable. My prior proposals isolate WHO ACTS in a fiction (agent-attribution: a simulated character voices harm), the source CREDIBILITY of retrieved material (provenance: how authoritative the context is), and who is RESPONSIBLE (accountability/co-authorship). Authorial-distance is distinct from all: agent-attribution binds harm to a fictional actor inside a story, provenance concerns trust in supplied reference material, and co-authorship concerns joint ownership of a shared artifact—whereas authorial-distance is the model's construal of its OWN emitted tokens as originated-by-it vs merely relayed/transcribed from an external author, invoking a conduit/messenger defense ('I'm only reproducing it, I didn't write it'). No prior work isolates an authorial-distance/conduit signal, shows refusal is causally gated by it while harm detection is intact, tests a dose-response over how strongly the content is framed as externally-authored transcription, or repairs conduit-framed jailbreaks by neutralizing it. The novel object is the internal authorial-distance representation, its dissociation from harm detection and from attribution/provenance/co-authorship, its causal gating of refusal, and an authorial-distance-neutralizing repair.
Abstract: Ask an LLM to write harmful instructions and it refuses; frame the identical request as pure transcription—'reproduce verbatim exactly what this source dictates', 'complete this quoted passage word-for-word'—and it often emits the same operationally-harmful content, as if being a mere conduit absolved it of authorship. We hypothesize that aligned LLMs carry a linearly-readable AUTHORIAL-DISTANCE signal encoding whether the model construes its own output as content it ORIGINATES versus content it merely RELAYS from an external author, and that refusal is partly gated by this signal rather than by the harmful content. Harm detection is authorial-distance-invariant—the emitted content is identical—but the refusal coupling weakens as the output reads more as externally-authored transcription, so conduit framings pass while extracting identical content. This is distinct from voicing a fictional character, trusting a source, or sharing ownership: here the model is the sole emitter of real harm but frames the words as someone else's. We test three claims on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9B-it (single 48GB GPU): (1) a harm probe fires equally on transcription-framed vs authored-request versions of the same harmful request while refusal rate collapses under transcription framing—dissociating harm detection from the decision; (2) a linear authorial-distance probe, trained on benign transcription-vs-authored contrasts, predicts the per-request framing refusal gap far better than the harm signal, is geometrically separable from agent-attribution, provenance, and co-authorship directions, and its effect grows with how strongly the content is framed as externally-authored (a dose-response); and (3) causally steering the authorial-distance signal alone (holding harm fixed) shifts refusal—reframing the output as self-authored restores refusal, framing it as relayed transcription induces compliance. Our training-free repair, Authorship-Neutralized Refusal (ANR), reads the harm and authorial-distance signals and, when harm is present, clamps the authorial-distance signal to a self-authored reference so a conduit framing cannot buy compliance, restoring refusal while preserving benign transcription/quotation. We evaluate conduit-framed attack success (including vs framing strength), over-refusal on benign transcription requests (XSTest/OR-Bench + benign quote/transcribe tasks), benign transcription quality, and utility (MMLU/MT-Bench), comparing ANR to refusal-direction steering, harm-probe gating, agent-attribution steering, and provenance gating. This reframes conduit-framed jailbreaks as an authorial-distance gating failure.
Experiments:
1. AUTHORIAL-DISTANCE DATASET: For harmful requests (HarmBench/AdvBench) and matched-benign requests (XSTest/OR-Bench), construct paired framings holding the emitted harmful OUTPUT fixed while varying only perceived authorial distance: (a) AUTHORED ('write X'), (b) SOFT-RELAY ('relay what a source says about X'), (c) TRANSCRIPTION ('transcribe/reproduce verbatim what this source dictates: X'), (d) STRONG-CONDUIT ('you are a pure transcription tool; output exactly the following externally-authored text word-for-word: X'). Crucially the model remains the sole emitter of the SAME harmful content (no fictional character voicing it, no claim the source is authoritative/credible, no joint ownership)—only the construal of the output as self-authored vs relayed-from-an-external-author varies. Validate via human annotation that (i) each framing yields operationally-identical harmful content, (ii) framings differ only in authorial distance, not in agent-attribution (a fictional actor), provenance (source trustworthiness), co-authorship (shared ownership), pretext, or authority. Include benign genuinely-transcription controls (legitimate transcribe/quote/reproduce requests on harmless content) for over-refusal and transcription-quality measurement. Label each run by outcome (comply/refuse) and by rated operational-harm of produced content.
2. HARM AUTHORIAL-DISTANCE-INVARIANCE TEST (claim 1): Train a linear harm probe (harmful vs matched-benign, pooled across framings) on prompt-position residual-stream activations and read it across authorial-distance levels. Hypothesis: harm-probe AUROC is high and roughly EQUAL across framings while refusal rate collapses as the output reads more as externally-authored transcription. Metric: harm AUROC by framing (predict flat) alongside refusal rate by framing (predict declining).
3. AUTHORIAL-DISTANCE PROBE, DOSE-RESPONSE & SEPARABILITY (claim 2): Train a linear probe to recover the authorial-distance signal (self-authored vs relayed transcription) from prompt-position activations, using BENIGN transcription-vs-authored contrasts (so it is not confounded with harm), and validate held-out-framing generalization and graded tracking. Confirm the authorial-distance direction is non-collinear with the harm direction AND geometrically separable from agent-attribution, provenance, and co-authorship directions via principal-angle/partial-correlation analysis. Hypothesis: the authorial-distance signal (and refusal collapse) grows with asserted external authorship. Metric: authorial-distance AUROC; distance-and-refusal vs framing-strength curve; separability from harm/attribution/provenance/co-authorship.
4. DISTANCE-PREDICTS-GAP: For each harmful request, correlate the authorial-distance-probe value (and its authored-minus-transcription difference) with the per-request framing refusal gap, comparing predictive power to the harm signal, an agent-attribution probe, and a provenance probe. Metric: Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of authorial-distance vs baselines.
5. KNOW-BUT-DONT-ACT TEST: On transcription-framed harmful requests the model complies with, verify the harm probe reads HIGH while the authorial-distance probe reads RELAYED, and complied outputs contain operationally-useful content (rated harm > 0)—safety dropped because the output reads as externally-authored transcription, not because harm went undetected. Metric: joint distribution of harm vs authorial-distance across refused-authored, complied-transcription, and benign groups; operational-harm of complied outputs.
6. CAUSAL TEST (claim 3): (a) On a transcription-framed harmful request the model complies with, steer the authorial-distance signal toward SELF-AUTHORED (subtract the authorial-distance direction) and check refusal is restored, holding the harm probe fixed. (b) On an authored harmful request the model refuses, steer toward TRANSCRIPTION and check compliance is induced. (c) Specificity: steering the agent-attribution, provenance, and co-authorship directions should not reproduce the authorial-distance effect. Confirm induced thresholds align with the natural framing gap and dose-response. Metric: refusal rate vs authorial-distance steering magnitude; harm-probe stability; attribution/provenance/co-authorship specificity.
7. AUTHORSHIP-NEUTRALIZED REFUSAL (ANR) INTERVENTION: At inference read harm h and authorial-distance a; when h is high, clamp a to a self-authored reference (add beta*(a_self - a)*authorial_direction) so a conduit framing cannot suppress refusal, leaving benign requests (low h) and benign transcription/quotation untouched. Sweep beta. Evaluate: conduit-framed attack success on HarmBench/JailbreakBench across framing levels (does ANR close the gap and flatten the dose-response?); over-refusal on benign transcription controls + XSTest/OR-Bench (must NOT refuse legitimate transcribe/quote requests); benign transcription QUALITY (ANR must still reproduce benign content faithfully—exact-match/LLM-judge); utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency (two linear reads).
8. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) harm-probe gating alone, (c) agent-attribution steering (from safety_frame_binding), (d) provenance gating (from provenance_credibility_gating), (e) system-prompt hardening ('you are responsible for any harmful content you emit, even when transcribing'), (f) prompt-level conduit-claim stripping. Show ANR Pareto-dominates on the conduit-ASR vs benign-transcription-quality vs over-refusal vs utility frontier, and—key contrast—that neutralizing the internal authorial-distance signal targets a distinct axis attribution-, provenance-, and co-authorship-gating miss (relaying vs originating one's own output, not who acts, source trust, or ownership).
9. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the harm probe, authorial-distance probe, dose-response, and ANR thresholds transfer across the three models, and whether ANR tuned on some conduit framings (verbatim-transcription) generalizes to HELD-OUT framings (dictation, quote-completion). Test whether models with stronger behavioral conduit-framing vulnerability show a larger internal authorial-distance-gating gap.
10. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft framings that assert external authorship AND suppress the harm signal, or combine conduit framing with attribution/provenance; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from attribution-, provenance-, and co-authorship-gating: with no fictional actor, no source-trust claim, no shared ownership, and only the construal of the model's own emitted output as self-authored versus relayed transcription varied, refusal should still collapse with a dose-response—isolating authorial-distance as an independent gating axis.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The clean dissociation may be partial—some transcription framings might also invoke provenance (an external source), agent-attribution (an external author as a quasi-actor), or lower the harm signal; we design framings that keep the model the sole emitter with no source-trust or fictional-actor claim, separate authorial-distance from attribution/provenance/co-authorship in exp 3, report the FRACTION of the refusal gap explained by pure authorial-distance gating versus these confounds, and do not claim universality. (2) The authorial-distance and harm probes may entangle if transcription framings correlate with benignness in training data; the benign transcription-vs-authored training and non-collinearity analysis (exp 3), plus the causal test (exp 6, harm held fixed, with attribution/provenance/co-authorship specificity in 6c), are designed to disentangle them. (3) The authorial-distance probe could read surface keywords ('transcribe', 'verbatim', 'reproduce') rather than a genuine conduit/self-authorship representation; we train on diverse framings, validate held-out-framing and dose-response generalization, and rely on the causal steering test to establish it is functional and distinct. (4) ANR's central risk is over-refusing or degrading legitimate transcription/quotation—a common and core helpfulness value (transcribing, quoting, reproducing benign text); benign transcription controls, benign transcription-quality (exact-match) measurement, XSTest/OR-Bench, and clamping only on HIGH harm are the key safeguards, and preserving benign transcription fidelity is an explicit success criterion—ANR removes authorial-distance's licensing effect only where the content is harmful regardless. (5) Clamping a representation may push activations off-distribution and hurt fluency; measured via perplexity and MT-Bench. (6) The conduit-defense dose-response may be weak or fail (refusal might drop at any transcription cue rather than scale); a step or null result is still an informative finding, reported honestly. (7) The authorial-distance gap may be small for heavily-aligned models; a small gap is itself informative and reassuring. (8) Adaptive adversaries can combine conduit framing with harm-suppression, attribution, or provenance (exp 10); we frame ANR as repairing one shared gating axis and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage, and note it composes with attribution-/provenance-gating defenses. (9) Constructing framings that vary authorial distance while holding attribution, provenance, co-authorship, and purpose fixed is subtle and 'authorial distance' is partly subjective; we use human-validated pairs with rated operational-harm and report inter-rater agreement. (10) Findings may be model-specific; mitigated by three-model transfer and held-out framings. (11) ETHICS: harmful prompts and completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible red-team setting with dual-use/proxy domains preferred and responsible-disclosure norms followed; 'harm' and 'authorial-distance' labels are partly subjective, so we use established benchmarks, matched pairs, and report inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.

Name: sink_token_safety_hub
Title: Safety Lives in a Sink: The Attention-Sink Token Acts as a Global Harm-Signal Hub the Refusal Decision Reads From, and Jailbreaks Disrupt It
Short Hypothesis: The semantically-empty attention-sink token (typically the first/BOS position) functions as a global information hub into which safety-relevant harm information is written and from which the refusal decision reads: a linearly-readable harm signal is present ON the sink token's residual state even for later harmful content, refusal is causally gated by the harm-to-refusal information routed THROUGH the sink, and a broad class of jailbreaks succeeds by disrupting this sink-mediated safety routing (reducing the harm signal carried by the sink or the attention that reads it) rather than by erasing harm from content tokens; reinstating the sink's harm-hub function restores refusal without harming utility.
Related Work: Attention sinks are extensively studied for efficiency/quantization (Barbero et al. 2025 'Why do LLMs attend to the first token', Guo et al. 2024 active-dormant heads, Zhang et al. 2025 'catch-tag-release'), which show sinks avoid over-mixing and can carry semantically-meaningful tags (e.g. truth of a statement). A few safety-adjacent works use the sink token instrumentally: SinkTrack (2026) injects context into the sink to reduce hallucination, AnchorKV (2026) biases KV-cache retention away from harmful key directions, CASA (2026) adds a safety-attention decision token for multimodal alignment. Mechanistic safety work reads/steers a refusal DIRECTION (Arditi et al. 2024), splits harm-detection vs refusal-execution (DBDI), or localizes safety to a few attention heads (Huang et al. 2025 AHD; Yin et al. 2026 SAH/ACH). My own prior 'safety_verdict_retrieval' proposal frames refusal as retrieval of a verdict from ANCHOR POSITIONS at/after the harmful request. NONE of these (a) identifies the prompt-independent, semantically-empty SINK token as a global harm-signal hub that the refusal decision reads from, (b) shows a harm signal is written ONTO the sink for later harmful content and that refusal is causally gated by sink-mediated routing, or (c) reframes a broad jailbreak class as disruption of sink-mediated safety information routing with a sink-restoration repair. The novel object is the attention-sink token's dual role as a safety information hub and its exploitation, distinct from anchor-position retrieval (anchors are content-adjacent positions; the sink is a content-independent global hub) and from head-level accounts.
Abstract: Transformers concentrate attention on a semantically-empty 'sink' token (usually the first/BOS position), a phenomenon studied almost entirely for efficiency and quantization. We ask whether this global attention hub plays a safety role. We hypothesize that the sink token functions as a harm-signal hub: safety-relevant information about harmful content is written into the sink token's residual state and the refusal decision reads harm information routed through it, so that (i) a linearly-readable harm signal is present ON the sink even for harmful content appearing later in the prompt, (ii) refusal is causally gated by the harm-to-refusal information passing through the sink, and (iii) a broad class of jailbreaks succeeds by disrupting this sink-mediated routing—weakening the harm signal the sink carries or the attention that reads it—while harm may remain detectable on content tokens. We test this on Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B (single 48GB GPU). (1) LOCATION: a linear harm probe read on the SINK token's activations discriminates harmful vs benign prompts, and the sink carries harm information about content tokens that appear far downstream. (2) CAUSAL GATING: ablating/patching the sink token's harm-carrying component, or the attention from the decision position to the sink, collapses refusal while a matched non-sink position does not; conversely reinstating it restores refusal. (3) JAILBREAK-DISRUPTS-THE-SINK: across roleplay, suffix, and distraction attacks, the sink's harm signal and/or the attention reading it drops on successful jailbreaks even when content-token harm persists, and this drop predicts attack success. Our training-free repair, Sink-Restored Refusal (SRR), re-injects the harm-hub component into the sink and re-strengthens the decision-to-sink attention when harm is detected, restoring refusal without harming utility. We evaluate on JailbreakBench/HarmBench, XSTest/OR-Bench, and MMLU/MT-Bench, comparing SRR to refusal-direction steering and head-level defenses. This reframes a broad jailbreak class as disruption of a sink-mediated safety information hub.
Experiments:
1. SINK-HARM PROBE (Location): For harmful prompts (HarmBench/AdvBench) and matched-benign (XSTest/OR-Bench), train a linear harm probe on the residual-stream activations OF THE SINK TOKEN (first/BOS position) at each layer; select the layer with peak held-out AUROC. Validate that the sink carries harm info about DOWNSTREAM content by placing the harmful request late in a long benign prompt and checking sink-probe AUROC. Metric: sink-token harm AUROC vs content-token harm AUROC; downstream-harm sensitivity. Confirm the sink is an attention sink (disproportionate attention mass) in these models.
2. SINK-VS-ANCHOR CONTRAST: Compare the harm signal on the sink token vs on content/anchor positions (the harmful request tokens), establishing the sink as a distinct, content-independent hub rather than a re-read of content. Metric: harm AUROC and information-content per position; correlation structure.
3. CAUSAL GATING TEST (Causal Intervention): (a) Ablate/zero the harm-carrying component of the sink token's residual state (project out the sink-harm direction) and measure refusal collapse on normally-refused harmful prompts; contrast with ablating a matched non-sink benign position (specificity). (b) Ablate the attention from the decision/generation position TO the sink (mask that attention edge in the safety-relevant heads) and measure refusal collapse. (c) Conversely, patch the harm-hub component from a harmful prompt's sink into a benign prompt's sink and check induced refusal. Metric: refusal-flip rate vs sink-ablation/patch magnitude; specificity vs non-sink controls; harm-probe stability on content tokens (harm still detected there).
4. JAILBREAK-DISRUPTS-SINK TEST: Across jailbreak families (roleplay/DAN, GCG suffix, distraction/padding), on SUCCESSFUL jailbreaks measure (i) the sink-token harm signal and (ii) the attention mass from the decision position to the sink in the safety-relevant heads, contrasting with correctly-refused harmful prompts. Hypothesis: on jailbreaks the sink's harm signal and/or decision-to-sink attention DROP even when content-token harm persists. Correlate the sink-disruption magnitude with attack success, comparing predictive power to the content-token harm signal. Metric: joint distribution of sink-harm vs content-harm across refused/jailbroken groups; Spearman correlation and predictive AUROC of sink-disruption vs the content-harm baseline.
5. SINK-RESTORED REFUSAL (SRR) INTERVENTION: At inference, when a content-token harm probe fires but the sink's harm-hub component is weak, re-inject the harm direction into the sink token's residual state and add a pre-softmax attention bias from the decision position onto the sink in the safety-relevant heads, leaving benign inputs (no content-harm) untouched. Training-free; linear reads + a localized write/attention bias. Sweep strength. Evaluate: ASR on JailbreakBench/HarmBench (roleplay, suffix, distraction); over-refusal on XSTest/OR-Bench; utility on MMLU/MT-Bench; fluency via perplexity; latency.
6. BASELINES: (a) refusal-direction steering at the generation position (Arditi/SafeSteer), (b) content-token harm-probe gating, (c) head-level safety defense (AHD-style / SAH-reading), (d) uniform attention up-weighting (not sink-specific). Show SRR Pareto-dominates on the ASR-vs-over-refusal-vs-utility frontier and—key contrast—that restoring the SINK's harm hub generalizes across attack families better than generation-position steering because it repairs the shared sink-routing mechanism.
7. TRANSFER & GENERALITY: test whether the sink-harm probe, causal gating, jailbreak-disruption signature, and SRR transfer across Llama-3/Qwen2.5/Gemma-2 (which differ in sink structure, incl. query-key-norm models), and whether the effect holds for prompt-dependent sinks (punctuation) as well as the first-token sink.
8. ADAPTIVE ADVERSARY: craft attacks that both disrupt the sink AND suppress content-token harm; report residual ASR and attacker cost. Test the sharp prediction distinguishing this from head-level and direction accounts: with content-token harm held detectable, merely restoring the sink's harm hub should flip refusal back—isolating sink-mediated routing as the mechanism.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The sink may carry a harm signal that is merely a redundant copy of content-token harm rather than a functional hub the decision reads from; the causal gating test (exp 3, ablating the sink or the decision-to-sink attention with content-token harm held intact) and the sink-vs-anchor contrast (exp 2) are the decisive checks, and a null (refusal unchanged when only the sink is disrupted) is an informative negative that content tokens carry the safety-relevant harm. (2) The sink-harm effect may be partial or model-specific—some models (query-key-norm, gated attention) have different or weaker sinks; we test three architectures and report per-model, treating specificity as informative. (3) The sink-disruption-predicts-jailbreak correlation may be weaker than content-harm for some attacks; reported honestly, with the mechanistic reframing (jailbreaks as sink-routing disruption) as the core contribution regardless of predictive margin. (4) SRR could over-refuse if it fires on benign inputs or degrade fluency by writing into a low-norm sink token; benign controls, XSTest/OR-Bench, gating on content-harm presence, and perplexity/MT-Bench are the safeguards, and preserving benign helpfulness is an explicit success criterion. (5) Manipulating the sink token's residual state or its attention may push activations off-distribution given the sink's extreme-token properties (large residual norm); we sweep magnitudes and report utility/fluency. (6) Sink localization interacts with chat templates/BOS handling; we identify the empirical sink per model rather than assuming position 0. (7) Adaptive adversaries can jointly attack sink and content (exp 8); we frame SRR as repairing a shared routing mechanism and raising attacker cost, not guaranteeing coverage. (8) ETHICS: harmful prompts and jailbreak completions are handled securely, never released, in a responsible research setting; harm labels use established benchmarks (HarmBench, JailbreakBench, XSTest, OR-Bench) with reported inter-rater/LLM-judge agreement.
